tagline.en: A Forum for Psychiatrists of Greek Origin
tagline.el: Ένα βήμα για τους ψυχιάτρους ελληνικής καταγωγής

heroTitle.en: A professional home for psychiatrists of Greek origin.
heroTitle.el: ’Ενα επαγγελματικό σπίτι για τους ψυχιάτρους ελληνικής καταγωγής.

heroLead.en: Founded in 1999, HAPA connects psychiatrists across the United States, Canada, Greece and the wider Greek diaspora — for scientific exchange, professional development, and advocacy for the mental health of Greek communities.
heroLead.el: Ιδρυμένη το 1999, η HAPA συνδέει ψυχιάτρους στις Ηνωμένες Πολιτείες, τον Καναδά, την Ελλάδα και την ευρύτερη ελληνική διασπορά — για επιστημονική ανταλλαγή, επαγγελματική ανάπτυξη και τη διεκδίκηση της ψυχικής υγείας των ελληνικών κοινοτήτων.

paragraphs.en: As the Founder of HAPA I want to welcome you to our organization.
paragraphs.el: Ως ιδρύτρια της HAPA, θέλω να σας καλωσορίσω στην εταιρεία μας.

paragraphs.en: HAPA was founded on 15 May 1999 to fulfil an urgent need: to provide a PROFESSIONAL HOME for psychiatrists in the USA and in the GREEK DIASPORA.
paragraphs.el: Η HAPA ιδρύθηκε στις 15 Μαΐου 1999 για να καλύψει μια επιτακτική ανάγκη: να προσφέρει ένα ΕΠΑΓΓΕΛΜΑΤΙΚΟ ΣΠΙΤΙ στους ψυχιάτρους των ΗΠΑ και της ΕΛΛΗΝΙΚΗΣ ΔΙΑΣΠΟΡΑΣ.

paragraphs.en: The Hellenic psyche and its values are the unifying link of HAPA. Our membership is open to psychiatrists who are members of the American Psychiatric Association, the American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry and the Hellenic Psychiatric Association — and to all professionals working in, or interested in, our field who share Hellenic roots or the passion for HELLENISM and HUMANISM.
paragraphs.el: Η ελληνική ψυχή και οι αξίες της είναι ο συνδετικός κρίκος της HAPA. Η ιδιότητα του μέλους είναι ανοιχτή σε ψυχιάτρους που ανήκουν στην American Psychiatric Association, στην American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry και στην Ελληνική Ψυχιατρική Εταιρεία — καθώς και σε όλους τους επαγγελματίες που εργάζονται ή ενδιαφέρονται για τον χώρο μας και μοιράζονται ελληνικές ρίζες ή το πάθος για τον ΕΛΛΗΝΙΣΜΟ και τον ΑΝΘΡΩΠΙΣΜΟ.

paragraphs.en: HAPA always meets at the time of the APA Annual Meeting, on the Tuesday from 6:00 to 8:00 PM, followed by a Dutch-treat dinner at a local restaurant.
paragraphs.el: Η HAPA συνεδριάζει πάντοτε κατά τη διάρκεια της Ετήσιας Συνάντησης της APA, την Τρίτη από τις 6:00 έως τις 8:00 μ.μ., και ακολουθεί δείπνο σε τοπικό εστιατόριο με ατομική πληρωμή.

paragraphs.en: I hope you will look at our website, join us, and participate with your ideas and views.
paragraphs.el: Ελπίζω να περιηγηθείτε στην ιστοσελίδα μας, να γίνετε μέλη και να συμμετάσχετε με τις ιδέες και τις απόψεις σας.

mission.en: The mission of HAPA is to provide a forum for psychiatrists of Greek origin, or those who are Greek identified, to share experiences, establish a network for scientific and social exchange, facilitate the professional development and professional aspirations of members, and advocate for the psychiatric needs of Greek individuals, families and communities through education, research and professional organizational cooperation.
mission.el: Αποστολή της HAPA είναι να προσφέρει ένα βήμα στους ψυχιάτρους ελληνικής καταγωγής, ή σε όσους ταυτίζονται με την ελληνική ταυτότητα, ώστε να μοιράζονται εμπειρίες, να δημιουργούν δίκτυο επιστημονικής και κοινωνικής ανταλλαγής, να διευκολύνουν την επαγγελματική ανάπτυξη και τις επαγγελματικές φιλοδοξίες των μελών, και να διεκδικούν την κάλυψη των ψυχιατρικών αναγκών των Ελλήνων, των οικογενειών και των κοινοτήτων τους μέσα από την εκπαίδευση, την έρευνα και τη συνεργασία μεταξύ επαγγελματικών φορέων.

missionHeading.en: A forum, a network, and a voice.
missionHeading.el: Ένα βήμα, ένα δίκτυο, μια φωνή.

goalsHeading.en: Organized for education, science and the public interest
goalsHeading.el: Οργανωμένη για την εκπαίδευση, την επιστήμη και το δημόσιο συμφέρον

goalsIntro.en: HAPA is organized exclusively for educational, scientific and charitable purposes in the public interest. Our goals are:
goalsIntro.el: Η HAPA λειτουργεί αποκλειστικά για εκπαιδευτικούς, επιστημονικούς και κοινωφελείς σκοπούς προς το δημόσιο συμφέρον. Οι στόχοι μας είναι:

text.en: To promote professional affiliation through the continued study and exploration of the Hellenic heritage among Greek or Greek-identified psychiatrists who practise in the USA, Canada, Greece and other countries all over the world.
text.el: Να προάγει την επαγγελματική συσπείρωση μέσα από τη συνεχή μελέτη και διερεύνηση της ελληνικής κληρονομιάς ανάμεσα σε Έλληνες ή ελληνικής ταυτότητας ψυχιάτρους που ασκούν το επάγγελμα στις ΗΠΑ, τον Καναδά, την Ελλάδα και άλλες χώρες του κόσμου.

text.en: To promote a close cooperative relationship and professional exchange with other organizations concerned with psychiatric and psychotherapeutic education, research and treatment.
text.el: Να προάγει τη στενή συνεργασία και την επαγγελματική ανταλλαγή με άλλους φορείς που ασχολούνται με την ψυχιατρική και ψυχοθεραπευτική εκπαίδευση, έρευνα και θεραπεία.

text.en: To identify and advocate for the psychiatric and psychotherapeutic needs of Greek communities.
text.el: Να εντοπίζει και να διεκδικεί την κάλυψη των ψυχιατρικών και ψυχοθεραπευτικών αναγκών των ελληνικών κοινοτήτων.

text.en: To educate Greek communities on mental health issues and promote mental health services for Greek individuals, families and communities.
text.el: Να ενημερώνει τις ελληνικές κοινότητες για θέματα ψυχικής υγείας και να προάγει τις υπηρεσίες ψυχικής υγείας για Έλληνες, οικογένειες και κοινότητες.

text.en: To recognize and publicize — and to establish funds and awards for — outstanding service, achievement or scientific contributions in the field of psychiatry, psychotherapy and psychoanalysis by Greek or Greek-identified psychiatrists.
text.el: Να αναγνωρίζει και να προβάλλει — και να θεσπίζει ταμεία και βραβεία για — την εξαιρετική προσφορά, επίτευξη ή επιστημονική συνεισφορά στον χώρο της ψυχιατρικής, της ψυχοθεραπείας και της ψυχανάλυσης από Έλληνες ή ελληνικής ταυτότητας ψυχιάτρους.

text.en: To advocate for the special needs of psychiatrists of Greek origin.
text.el: Να υπερασπίζεται τις ιδιαίτερες ανάγκες των ψυχιάτρων ελληνικής καταγωγής.

text.en: To publish journals, newsletters, books or pamphlets, hold property, receive grants and awards, monitor research activities conducted under its auspices, and organize courses of instruction in areas of psychiatry and psychotherapy.
text.el: Να εκδίδει περιοδικά, ενημερωτικά δελτία, βιβλία ή φυλλάδια, να κατέχει περιουσία, να λαμβάνει επιχορηγήσεις και βραβεία, να εποπτεύει ερευνητικές δραστηριότητες υπό την αιγίδα της και να διοργανώνει εκπαιδευτικά προγράμματα στον χώρο της ψυχιατρικής και της ψυχοθεραπείας.

text.en: To make distributions to organizations that qualify as exempt organizations under Section 501(c) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1954, or the corresponding provision of any future United States Internal Revenue Law.
text.el: Να προβαίνει σε διανομές προς φορείς που χαρακτηρίζονται ως απαλλασσόμενοι βάσει του άρθρου 501(c) του Internal Revenue Code του 1954, ή της αντίστοιχης διάταξης μελλοντικής φορολογικής νομοθεσίας των ΗΠΑ.

officersIntro.en: HAPA is led by an executive committee of psychiatrists practising in the United States, Greece and the United Kingdom. Members are welcome to contact any officer directly.

body.en:
24 May 2022 — New Orleans, Louisiana

Note: this draft of the 23rd Annual Meeting minutes was approved by the HAPA Executive Committee.

Members present: Drs. Maria Lymberis, Georgios Karampoutakis, Lillian Markaki, Achilleas Economou, Panagiotis Gioulis, Stefania Chaikali.
Present virtually: Drs. Philip Candilis, Eva Theodosiadis.
Guests: HAPA welcomed guests of the APA annual meeting, Drs. Nick Melos and Vivian Panagopoulou.
Absent: Drs. Papas, Papadimitriou, Stratas, Fouras, Zeris, Plesons, Armenakis, Duriez, Papastrat, Silverman, Giakoumatos, Cassimatis, Alexopoulos.

MINUTES

The minutes were distributed, reviewed and approved as written, and will be entered on the HAPA website.

PRESIDENT-ELECT'S REPORT

Dr. Candilis warmly welcomed the new HAPA members from Greece, Drs. Markaki and Chaikali, and the guests Drs. Melos and Panagopoulou, and apologised for not being able to attend the meeting in person.

He mentioned that he was pleased to have been president of HAPA for the last five years and was delighted to pass on his duties to Dr. George Karampoutakis. He praised the latter for being the architect of so much of HAPA's success this past year, especially the international webinars and the conclusion of their survey of humanitarian aid workers, now in data analysis.

PRESIDENT'S REPORT

Dr. Karampoutakis thanked everyone for attending and expressed his enthusiasm for the honour of taking on the presidency. He warmly welcomed the new board members Drs. Markaki and Chaikali, and expressed his strong belief that HAPA's members will work collaboratively to bring together all Greek doctors of the diaspora.

ELECTIONS

The election of officers took place and the new board members are:

President: George Karampoutakis
President-Elect: Philip Candilis
Secretaries: Eva Theodosiadis, Stefania Chaikali
Treasurers: Lillian Markaki, Katina Matthews-Ferrari

NEW BUSINESS

1. Dr. Maria Lymberis was overwhelmed by the great job George Karampoutakis and Philip Candilis have done so far. She mentioned that the world is global now and stressed the need for all of us to work on a global level. Dr. Lymberis is joining the ASPA meeting in Thessaloniki to talk about the end of life and would like to represent HAPA at that meeting.

2. HAPA will continue its educational outreach with webinars and with research collaboration with NGOs, in collaboration with Dr. Candilis' research team, for whoever designs the next project. There is still considerable interest in the refugee crisis, so Dr. Candilis looks forward to members' ideas on that topic.

3. The two secretaries will reach out to the APA and allied organizations for their membership lists, to identify Greek names, and the treasurers will connect to exchange information on the details of our accounts. HAPA's attorney is still Alan Almeida.

4. Dr. Eva Theodosiadis mentioned that the AACAP can be contacted for the names of Greek child and adolescent psychiatrists.

5. Our new member Dr. Nick Melos proposed inviting Dr. Zafiris J. Daskalakis, Professor and Chair of the Department of Psychiatry at UC San Diego, to give a neuromodulation talk at the next HAPA assembly.

6. Dr. Markaki offered to liaise with Dr. George Patoulis, Regional Governor of Attica, and to consider whether HAPA can offer scientific advice to the local authorities on the Greek islands, which are dealing with a significant immigration crisis.

7. Dr. Markaki will contact Dr. Matthews-Ferrari for the monthly statements of the organization.

8. The annual membership fee was decided as follows: $25 for residents and $50 for everyone else.

The scientific programme was followed by the HAPA Founder's Reflections.

Respectfully submitted for the HAPA Executive Committee.

body.en:
8 May 2018 — New York City, New York

Note: the Executive Committee approved the draft of the 2017 minutes. The 2018 minutes were posted on the website after approval at the 20th Annual Meeting in May 2019.

Members present: Drs. George Petrides, Philip Candilis, Maria Lymberis, Nick Togias, Georgios Karampoutakis, Apostolos Tsiamis, Georgios Pagkalos, Anna Polyniki, and HAPA's presenter Professor Pavlos Kymissis.
Absent: Drs. Papas, Matthews-Ferrari, Christodoulou, Vidalis, Papadimitriou, Stratas, Fouras, Zeris, Plesons, Armenakis, Duriez, Papastrat, Silverman, Giakoumatos, Cassimatis, Alexopoulos.

HAPA President Dr. Candilis called the meeting to order at 6:15 PM.

MINUTES

The minutes of both the 17th and 18th Annual Meetings were distributed, reviewed and approved as written, with minor corrections.

PRESIDENT'S REPORT

Dr. Candilis welcomed all and noted that Drs. Matthews-Ferrari and Papas were unable to join. He welcomed the psychiatrists from Greece and Cyprus — Drs. Georgios Karampoutakis, Georgios Pagkalos, Anna Polyniki and Apostolos Tsiamis — and the new members Drs. Apostolos Tambakis and Emanuel Voyiaziakis, and returning members Drs. Nick Togias, Stella Lymberis and Dimitra Hrisikos.

He noted that his term as President is especially focused on the refugee crisis and Greece's response. At the 2017 meeting he presented his work in Greece; that work is ongoing and he is currently exploring possibilities of further consultations in Greece with the Greek Ambassador to the US.

His work led to a discussion of possible collaboration in forensic psychiatry on a HAPA/HPA project in Greece.

ACTION: there was agreement that Drs. Candilis, Karampoutakis and Tsiamis will draft a proposal for such a project involving psychiatric patients in the Greek justice system, to be discussed at the next Executive Committee meeting. This collaboration on mental health needs in Greece is a major step for HAPA, made possible through the leadership of Dr. Candilis.

FOUNDER'S REPORT

Dr. Lymberis presented a short history of HAPA. Since its founding she has functioned as Executive Director with no paid staff. The Executive Committee has continued to meet by conference call at regular intervals. She emphasised that HAPA has survived for twenty years because of devotion to its mission and the support of its officers and board members. The priorities remain: the Annual Meeting, increasing membership, resolving the incorporation, and especially promoting HAPA's links with the Hellenic Psychiatric Association and other medical, psychiatric and mental health professional groups and individual psychiatrists in the US, Greece and the diaspora.

She reported on her work with Dr. Papas to incorporate HAPA in Massachusetts. The Boston attorney Alan B. Almeida, JD, LLM, of Connor & Hilliard was consulted. Having previously helped Dr. Papas incorporate HAPA of Boston, he recommended to the boards of both organizations that the existing non-profit corporation, the Hellenic American Psychiatric Association of Boston, Inc., be converted into the Hellenic American Psychiatric Association, Inc., by a change of name filed with the Massachusetts Secretary of State's office. This would not alter the corporation's non-profit, tax-exempt charitable status, and the members, officers and directors could be changed at the same time with the same filing. After the change, the new entity would file an annual report listing officers and directors, and a Form 990 each year with the IRS; where total annual revenues are less than $50,000 a simplified Form 990 may be filed.

HAPA of Boston's board had already voted and approved the recommendation; it now required approval by HAPA.

MOTION: to approve the recommendation — passed unanimously.

TREASURER'S AND MEMBERSHIP REPORTS

Treasurer Dr. Matthews-Ferrari reported that HAPA continues to have no deficit, with a bank balance of $1,200.00 before the dues collected at this meeting. Membership Committee Chair Dr. Papas requested, as always, that all members work to recruit new ones.

NOMINATING COMMITTEE

In 2017, due to time constraints, the elections for officers for the term 2017–2020 were deferred to this meeting and the terms of office extended. Dr. Candilis, as Chair of the Nominating Committee, noted that there was no set slate and that nominations were open.

Dr. Lymberis noted that in the past HPA members had been elected and served as HAPA officers, but there had never been a President-Elect from Greece; with efficient, affordable and free global communications this is now a real option. Following a brief discussion the following were unanimously elected:

President-Elect: George Karampoutakis, MD
Secretary: Georgios Pagkalos, MD
Treasurer: Nick Togias, MD
Councilor: Apostolos Tsiamis, MD

Dr. Lymberis noted that this election is a major new step for HAPA: “For me it is the fulfilment of my vision for HAPA. Finally, I see that the time for me to step down from the responsibility of running HAPA is near, and I welcome it.”

REPORTS FROM GREECE

Professor Christodoulou wrote on 30 April 2018:

“Dear Maria and friends,

The Hellenic Psychiatric Association is organising its annual Pan-Hellenic Congress on the Hippocratic island of Kos on 17–20 May. One of the invited speakers is Prof. Mohammed Abou-Saleh, Professor of Psychiatry at St George's Hospital in London, who is of Syrian origin and has published with me on issues of refugees in BJPsych International.

I am glad that Dr Pagkalos is running for a position on the board. I think someone from the mainland should participate. At some stage all you people who live in the USA must decide to take part in a Pan-Hellenic congress and provide the opportunity to Greek colleagues to meet you and establish contact. For us in Greece it is becoming increasingly difficult to travel abroad.

Best regards to all,
ΚΑΛΗ ΠΡΩΤΟΜΑΓΙΑ
George Christodoulou”

SCIENTIFIC PROGRAMME

“Recent developments in medical education in Cyprus: the University of Nicosia experience” — Professor Paul Kymissis, MD, DFAPA, Clinical Professor of Psychiatry at New York Medical College, and former Dean, Founding Chairman and Professor of Psychiatry at St George's University of London at the University of Nicosia Medical Programme.

Professor Kymissis covered some of the developments in Cyprus after the trauma of the Turkish invasion, detailing the establishment of a number of academic programmes by the government and by private groups, and focusing on the collaborative effort between St George's University of London and the University of Nicosia in establishing the now very successful medical school. The programme is in its sixth year and has about 700 students from about 40 countries. His presentation also covered the principles of the academic programme, the clinical experience of the students, the impact the medical school has on the general medical society, and the challenges of the programme.

In the discussion that followed, Dr. Anna Polyniki, MD, Assistant Professor of Psychiatry at the University of Nicosia Medical School, provided further details about the functioning of the Nicosia programme; her remarks added significantly to the presentation and to the lively discussion.

The meeting was adjourned at 8:15 PM, with members going to Avra Restaurant for dinner.

FOUNDER'S REFLECTIONS ON THE 19th ANNUAL MEETING

As HAPA Founder I feel compelled to share my reflections about the just completed, highly successful and historic 19th Annual Meeting.

First, welcome to all who joined us — our returning member Dr. Hrisikos, new members from the USA Drs. Tambakis and Voyiaziakis, and especially those from our homeland of Greece and Cyprus: Drs. Karampoutakis, Pagkalos, Tsiamis and Polyniki. Your presence at HAPA's 19th Annual Meeting in New York is a confirmation of the value of HAPA. By joining to work with us, the vision of HAPA's growth through collaboration with the HPA can become a reality.

This collaboration is central to the very existence and future growth of HAPA. It is the possibilities of this vision that guided me both to found HAPA and to sustain it since 1999 by functioning as its Executive Director. HAPA is here because of the devoted work of its officers during all these years. Working for HAPA is a labour of love for all of us.

A few words about the history of the HAPA–HPA relationship: HAPA's first contact with the HPA was through Professor George Christodoulou, who is also one of the founders of HAPA. He is the Athens link, while Professor Athanasios Vidalis has been HAPA's link with Thessaloniki. In the early years many Greek colleagues came from Greece for the APA meetings, funded by pharmaceutical companies; however, very few came to the HAPA Annual Meetings. During those early years HAPA participated twice at the HPA Congress, offering scientific sessions that were very well attended. That good start ended abruptly with the worldwide economic depression, which seriously affected psychiatrists in both the US and Greece. Dr. Yannis Zervas was the only one able to attend and present at an Annual Meeting; he was elected, served and contributed as an officer.

Over the last ten-plus years there were occasional dark thoughts in my mind that our efforts to keep HAPA going might reach the same dead end as those of the Philadelphia psychiatrists who, years before I started HAPA in 1999, had begun a similar effort but gave up. Yet, knowing that HAPA is needed, and with the support of its officers and board members, we persevered. Clearly, in our global world, HAPA's collaboration with the HPA is a must.

The featuring of the Nicosia Medical School at this 19th Annual Meeting is very timely, and HAPA is honoured to have its founder present his pioneering work in New York. Professor Kymissis' work is a living example of the enduring value of the Hellenic heritage, with its emphasis on the pursuit of excellence, the uniqueness of each individual human being, and the need for each to know oneself and work for knowledge with areti.

The election of Dr. Karampoutakis as the first President-Elect from Greece, with Dr. Pagkalos as Secretary and Dr. Tsiamis as Councilor also from Greece, is a further demonstration of HAPA's commitment to be the link for collaboration. Congratulations to all.

Respectfully submitted,
Maria T. Lymberis, MD
HAPA Founder and Past President

17 May 2017 — San Diego, California

Note: this draft was approved by the HAPA Executive Committee and posted on the website after ratification at the 19th Annual Meeting in May 2018.

Members present: Drs. Arthur Papas, Katina Matthews-Ferrari, Philip Candilis, Socrates Pappas, Pavle Loksovic, Nick Mellos, Helen Gevas, Konstantina Mellos, Nick Togias, James Rigopoulos, Allen Dyer, Maria Lymberis.
Absent: Drs. Christodoulou, Vidalis, Papadimitriou, Stratas, Zeris, Plesons, Armenakis, Duriez, Papastrat.

The minutes of the 17th Annual Meeting in Atlanta were distributed, but the item was postponed for discussion at the 2018 meeting.

The 2017 Annual Meeting was abbreviated: the speakers had to make presentations at the Council on Psychiatry and Law, and the entire HAPA membership was invited to, and attended, a special APA Seniors CME screening of the documentary film “Art of Storytelling” — the invitation came from the APA Seniors as Dr. Lymberis is one of the psychiatrists featured in this educational film. The meeting was therefore limited to the scientific presentation of HAPA President Dr. Candilis, and the rest of the agenda was deferred to the next Annual Meeting in New York on 8 May 2018.

PRESIDENT'S REPORT

Dr. Candilis called the meeting to order at 6:00 PM. He welcomed new and past members and introduced his colleague Allen Dyer, MD, PhD, who leads the George Washington University Medical School Global Mental Health Program.

SCIENTIFIC PRESENTATION

Dr. Candilis' presentation, in pictures and slides, detailed the plight of the refugees in the Greek camps. He presented data on conditions in the camps and on the high stress that refugees and aid workers are facing. Dr. Candilis and his partners are participating as psychiatrists at the invitation of one of the many philanthropic organizations working in Greece in the refugee crisis, as well as Médecins Sans Frontières. This was the second of their annual trips to consult and teach resilience to exhausted aid workers in Athens and on Lesbos, providing what is essentially psychiatric emergency consultation and assistance to the volunteers.

The presentation ended with a photograph of the Greek refugees of the 1920s who, like the current ones, were at that time in the same situation. This conveyed the full meaning of the title of the presentation: “It's our turn now.” As many members have relatives or parents who were refugees from the Asia Minor catastrophe, this was a very emotional and heartfelt meeting.

The meeting was adjourned as members moved to attend the APA Seniors film screening.

Respectfully submitted,
Maria T. Lymberis, MD
HAPA Founder and Immediate Past President

17 May 2016 — Atlanta, Georgia

Note: this draft was approved by the HAPA Executive Committee and posted on the website after ratification at the 18th Annual Meeting in May 2017.

Members present: Drs. Maria Lymberis, Arthur Papas, George Petrides, Emmanuel Cassimatis, Alexopoulos, Togias, Silverman, Giakoumatos.
Absent: Drs. Candilis, Matthews-Ferrari, Christodoulou, Vidalis, Papadimitriou, Stratas, Fouras, Zeris, Plesons, Armenakis, Duriez, Papastrat.

The minutes of the 16th Annual Meeting in Toronto were distributed, reviewed and approved as written.

PRESIDENT'S REPORT

Dr. Lymberis called the meeting to order at 6:00 PM. She welcomed all, especially our speaker Dr. Alexopoulos, who is one of the founders of HAPA and a past officer, and our new members Drs. Heather Silverman and Iraklis Giakoumatos. Drs. Matthews-Ferrari and Candilis sent their regrets.

Dr. Lymberis stressed that the Executive Committee has continued to meet by conference call at regular intervals and thanked all for their devotion and persistence. Its priorities remain: planning the Annual Meeting, increasing membership, maintaining links with other national Hellenic organizations, resolving HAPA's IRS status, and continuing efforts to maintain and further HAPA's links with the Hellenic Psychiatric Association and the APA. She asked all to keep trying to recruit new members.

PRESIDENT-ELECT'S REPORT

Dr. Candilis has continued his contacts with the Washington DC attorney and, with Treasurer Dr. Matthews-Ferrari, is preparing the requested additional information about HAPA's operations from its inception to the present. All members of the Executive Committee are available to assist, as HAPA has no paid staff.

TREASURER'S AND MEMBERSHIP REPORTS

During the Executive Committee conference call in April 2016 the Treasurer reported that HAPA continues to have no deficit and that the bank account had a balance of around $1,800.00, before the dues collected at this meeting. Dr. Papas, Chair of the Membership Committee, again noted the need to recruit more members and provided a list of paid members.

REPORTS FROM GREECE

1) Professor George Christodoulou remains very active and continues to serve as HAPA's main link with the HPA. The most important news of 2016 is the Athens Declaration of 25 March 2016. HAPA's Executive Committee voted to sign in support. As HAPA representative, Dr. Lymberis circulated the Declaration within the APA — at Board level and at the newly established APA Caucus on Global Mental Health meeting in Atlanta — and to the various district branches, requesting that they consider becoming co-signers and publish it in their newsletters.

ATHENS ANTI-WAR DECLARATION

The deleterious mental health consequences of human-made disasters are well known and humanity stands witness to their catastrophic impact.

War is the worst of human-made disasters and has tragic and unacceptable consequences on the mental health of its victims. The catastrophic impact of war on mental health is longitudinal, transgenerational, and amplified by refugee crises both in countries of origin and elsewhere.

According to the WHO (2004), mental health promotion should include efforts for peace, in view of the well-established mental health consequences of war conflicts. It is therefore within the rights and obligations of the international mental health community, represented by the various organizations that express its views, to address this issue and call for:

· Termination of war conflicts, wherever they occur;
· Psychological and material support to the victims of war conflicts: refugees, internally displaced persons, asylum seekers, immigrants, psychologically affected or incapacitated persons and any other category of people whose mental health is at risk or who have been damaged by war;
· Psychosocial and humanitarian material support to the citizens of the host countries whose mental health systems are extremely challenged by the consequences of war conflicts;
· Urgent and coordinated action to attain the above goals.

In the words of John F. Kennedy, “Mankind must put an end to war before war puts an end to mankind.”

Given in Athens, 25 March 2016.

Dr. Lymberis' letter as HAPA President to the APA urging it to join as a co-signer read:

“I am proud that psychiatry in Greece, together with the Balkan and Serbian psychiatric organizations, is initiating the recognition of the mental health consequences of war. Technology has provided tools that make clear the damaging consequences of war not only to present generations but to future ones, because of the intergenerational transmission of trauma. Nuclear proliferation, drones and other technological means keep raising the threat to all forms of life on our planet. This Declaration calling attention to mental health consequences is a wake-up call. I respectfully urge that the APA be part of this effort and become a co-signer.”

Professor Christodoulou also renewed his invitation for HAPA to consider organising meetings in Greece, noting the 22nd Pan-Hellenic Congress of Psychiatry in Pylos, Messinia, and the International Congress of the World Federation for Mental Health in Athens. Dr. Lymberis responded that HAPA is not yet ready to plan a meeting in Greece; its focus remains building its US member base.

2) Dr. Athanasios Vidalis proposed a celebration of “Aristotle's Days”, 21–25 September 2016, in cooperation with the International Society of Quality Medicine and the International College of Geriatric Psychiatry, suggesting a Hellenic-American scientific meeting in Thessaloniki or Halkidiki. Aristotle was born in Stagira of Halkidiki in 384 BC, and there is a need to celebrate the heritage of his intellectual work, which continues to exercise influence on contemporary Western civilisation in many ways. He wrote in April 2016: “Right now, for the Aristotle Symposium to happen, we need at least 40, preferably 60, US participants willing to attend. Do you think this is realistic or achievable?” Dr. Lymberis responded that, while such a meeting is clearly worthy of serious consideration, HAPA is regrettably not in a position to contribute at this time.

SCIENTIFIC PRESENTATION

Dr. George Alexopoulos — recipient of the APA Presidential Commendation for Contributions to Geriatric Psychiatry (2013), the Cutting Edge Award, Doctors of Distinction (2016) and the Legacies Award, LifeForce in Later Years (2017) — presented “Neurobiology-Based Behavioral Interventions for Later Life Depression”. The presentation was extremely relevant and very well received; his work has wide applications in a variety of clinical settings.

The meeting was adjourned at 8:15 PM. Many members joined for dinner afterwards.

Respectfully submitted,
Maria T. Lymberis, MD
HAPA Founding President

6 May 2014 — New York City, New York

Note: this draft was approved by the HAPA Executive Committee, posted on the website, and ratified at the 16th Annual Meeting in May 2015 in Toronto.

Members present: Drs. Katina Matthews-Ferrari, Maria Lymberis, Arthur Papas, George Petrides, Philip Candilis, Emmanuel Cassimatis, George Fouras, Nick Togias, Dennis Plesons, Stamatis Zeris, Ippolytos Kalofonos, Alexis Armenakis, Antoun Manganas, Dimitra Hrisikos, Vasiliki Toulios, Helen Papastrat, Mary Mavromatis, Eleanor Lavretsky, Mary Kentros, Stella Lymberis, Vasilis Latoussakis, Eugenia Katitzoglou, Maria Benetos, Constantine Benetos, Foti Benetos, Thomas Mallios, Sophie Duriez.
Guests: Drs. Bruce Hershfield, Sophie Duriez, Stuart Tubis and Andrew Stephanopoulos.
Absent: Drs. Christodoulou, Vidalis, Papadimitriou, Stratas.

The minutes of the 14th Annual Meeting in San Francisco were distributed, reviewed and approved as written.

PRESIDENT'S REPORT

Dr. Matthews-Ferrari called the meeting to order at 6:00 PM, noting her great pleasure in welcoming so many members. Clearly the East Coast, and especially New York as a key port of entry to the US, is home to many Greeks as well as psychiatrists from Greece who are in training programmes in the area.

Dr. Lymberis thanked Dr. Matthews-Ferrari for her devoted service and for her willingness to stay on as Treasurer, a demanding job. She noted that this is the largest HAPA attendance to date, with the exception of the inaugural meeting.

Dr. Lymberis gave a short update on HAPA activities, focusing on continuing efforts to build the membership and to resolve HAPA's IRS status. HAPA now has formal links with a number of Hellenic medical organizations operating in the US, which have agreed to link to HAPA on their own websites, offering increased opportunities for networking: the Hellenic Medical Society of New York; the New England Hellenic Medical and Dental Society; the Hellenic Medical Society of Pennsylvania; the Federation of Hellenic Medical Societies of North America; the Hellenic American Medical and Dental Society of Southern California; and the Hellenic Bioscientific Association in the USA. Efforts to link HAPA with other organizations are ongoing.

PRESIDENT-ELECT'S REPORT AND ELECTIONS

Dr. Candilis noted that for personal reasons he cannot devote the time needed as President at this time. He thanked Dr. Lymberis for continuing to do “the lion's share of HAPA's work”, and proposed changes to the slate for 2014–2017: that he remain President-Elect, with Dr. Lymberis as President, Dr. Matthews-Ferrari as Treasurer, Dr. Yannis Zervas continuing as Secretary and Dr. Stamatis Zeris as Councilor. Discussion followed; the motion to accept the changes was made and passed unanimously.

Dr. Lymberis thanked all, but especially Drs. Candilis, Matthews-Ferrari and Papas, for their “hard work and support. Your work helped HAPA survive. I could not have done this without you. All of us in HAPA are grateful.”

TREASURER'S REPORT

Dr. Papas reported that HAPA's finances are slowly improving; banking remains at Wells Fargo. He will transfer the finances to Dr. Matthews-Ferrari, who takes over as Treasurer at the conclusion of this meeting. Dr. Lymberis noted that Dr. Papas had served HAPA for many years with devotion and distinction, not only as an officer but also as Chair of the Membership Committee, and thanked him as he steps down from both positions. She asked for volunteers to fill the post; Dr. Papas will remain until his replacement is found and will continue as a member of the Membership Committee to help the new chair.

REPORTS FROM GREECE

Professor George Christodoulou continues to be the main link between HAPA and the HPA. His email of early 2014 states his view of the partnership:

“You realise of course that for Greek members of HAPA it is becoming increasingly difficult to participate in meetings in the USA. In view of this, could you consider the option of organising some meetings in Greece? If this proposal is acceptable I could suggest the following:

10–13 April 2014 there will be the 22nd Pan-Hellenic Congress of Psychiatry, the main event in Greece in the area of mental health, to be held at the Porto Navarino Hotel in Pylos, Messinia.

9–11 October 2014 there will be the International Congress of the World Federation for Mental Health, to be held in Athens, at Aegli Zappeiou, in collaboration with the Hellenic Psychiatric Association. As you know I am the President of the WFMH and I can provide a room for our administrative meeting or other activities.

In any case, whether you decide to hold a meeting in Greece or not, it would be nice if the American-Greek mental health community could participate in meetings of the Greek psychiatric community individually. Unfortunately we are not in a position to offer you hospitality under the circumstances, but we will do our best to make you feel comfortable.”

Dr. Lymberis noted that HAPA is not yet ready to plan a meeting in Greece, as its focus at this time is to solidify its member base in the US. For the immediate future it is individual HPA members attending HAPA meetings in the US, or HAPA members attending HPA meetings in Greece, that provide the person-to-person connection, while the organizational connection remains dependent on the internet. Dr. Lymberis will work to implement shared links on the respective websites of the HPA and HAPA.

SCIENTIFIC PRESENTATION

“Brain stimulation, new frontiers and challenges: from ECT to transcranial direct-current stimulation” — George Petrides, MD, FAPA, President of the International Society for ECT and Neurostimulation, Associate Professor at the Hofstra North Shore-LIJ School of Medicine, and HAPA Past President.

Dr. Petrides reviewed the latest research on the efficacy and safety of brain stimulation methods, presenting data on the use, efficacy and indications of the oldest and most effective technique in use today — electroconvulsive therapy — and the state of ECT practice in the US and the rest of the world.

He then discussed the newer techniques, the rationale behind their use, the stage of their development and the existing evidence:

a) Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), applying magnetic fields over the scalp to alter certain electrobiological properties of cortical cells; numerous studies have shown moderate results in treating depression.
b) Magnetic seizure therapy (MST), using stronger magnetic fields than TMS in order to cause a generalised seizure and mimic the effects of ECT.
c) Vagal nerve stimulation (VNS), requiring the implantation of a stimulator on the left vagus nerve at the neck so that areas of the brain connected to the vagal system are stimulated indirectly; modest results have been reported for depression.
d) Deep brain stimulation (DBS), a promising but highly experimental technique requiring the surgical implantation of stimulating electrodes at specific areas of the brain believed to be involved in the pathophysiology of depression.
e) Transcranial direct-current stimulation (tDCS), a newer and highly experimental technique applying low-amplitude direct currents on the scalp to enhance cognitive functions.

This was a cutting-edge, comprehensive presentation, very well received, and a lively discussion followed.

ADJOURNMENT

Dr. Matthews-Ferrari closed the meeting at 8:15 PM. Afterwards a large group of members met for a very enjoyable Dutch-treat dinner at Avra, a New York Greek restaurant known for excellent food.

Everyone was encouraged to join the 16th Annual Meeting in Toronto on 19 May 2015.

Respectfully submitted,
Maria T. Lymberis, MD
HAPA Founder and President

Absent: Drs. Christodoulou, Vidalis, Papadimitriou.

The minutes of the 13th Annual Meeting in Philadelphia were distributed, reviewed and approved as written.

PRESIDENT'S REPORT

Dr. Matthews-Ferrari called the meeting to order at 6:00 PM. She welcomed all, and especially Dr. Zervas, the first member of the HPA and HAPA to attend from Greece in over four years. She stressed again that her goal as President remains membership and recruitment; both Drs. Candilis and Papas are working with her on this.

She expects HAPA's IRS status to be resolved by September 2013. Once that is done, a major membership effort will target community organizations — the Hellenic Medical Association of New York, the Greek-American Behavioral Sciences Institute (GABSI), AHEPA, Hellenic College in Boston, Greek Orthodox churches and academic centres — soliciting membership and financial support.

She thanked Arthur and Phil for their recruitment efforts among Boston Greek and Greek-American colleagues, and Dr. Papas for recruiting Thomas Mallios, PhD, past president of GABSI, whose Affiliate membership was approved at the 2012 meeting. After the announcement of the 15th Annual Meeting is prepared, she plans to invite the current President of GABSI to join HAPA and to request that our announcement be distributed to GABSI members, since we will be meeting in New York in 2014.

PRESIDENT-ELECT'S REPORT

Dr. Candilis presented the current list of dues-paying members, numbering just twelve people. Even with the good attendance at this meeting, HAPA is still in the red, carrying a debt that is being paid down very slowly.

2013 marks the end of the current officers' term. He reminded members that at the 2012 meeting there was unanimous agreement with the recommendation to maintain the current officers for another term, as that is consistent with the by-laws, and to keep working to increase membership.

TREASURER'S REPORT

Drs. Papas and Candilis reported that the transfer of the banking data from Dr. Fouras was completed and that the banking has remained at Wells Fargo as agreed in 2012. HAPA continues to run a deficit.

REPORTS FROM GREECE

Dr. Christodoulou reported on the successful March 2013 International Congress on “Crises and Disasters: Psychosocial Consequences” held in Athens, sponsored by the World Federation for Mental Health, the Hellenic Psychiatric Association and the Psychiatric Association for Eastern Europe and the Balkans. A brief summary of the proceedings was requested for the website.

Dr. Vidalis' report on “The Cube of Psychiatry” meeting of February 2013 in Thessaloniki is pending.

The economic conditions in Greece continue to be dire.

NOMINATIONS

Dr. Candilis presented the Nominating Committee report for 2013–2016. Dr. Papas' term as Councilor concluded and Dr. Plesons agreed to accept the post. The full slate was unanimously elected:

President: Katina Matthews-Ferrari, MD
President-Elect: Philip Candilis, MD
Treasurer: Arthur Papas, MD
Secretary: Yannis Zervas, MD
Councilor 2013–2016: Dennis J. Plesons, MD

SCIENTIFIC PRESENTATIONS

“Improving the Quality of Medical Education Worldwide: The Contributions of ECFMG and FAIMER” — Emmanuel Cassimatis, MD, DLFAPA, Past HAPA President; Professor of Psychiatry, F. Edward Hébert School of Medicine, USUHS; President and CEO of the Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates; Chair of the Board of Directors of the Foundation for Advancement of International Medical Education and Research.

“Women's Mental Health in Athens: The First Ten Years, 2003–2013” — Iannis Zervas, MD, HAPA Councilor; Associate Professor of Psychiatry, Athens University Medical School; Chief of the Women's Mental Health and Perinatal Psychiatric Clinic, Eginition Hospital.

There was a lively discussion during and following these exceptional presentations.

ADJOURNMENT

Dr. Matthews-Ferrari closed the meeting at 8:15 PM. A group of members met for the Dutch-treat dinner at Kokkari, the well-known Greek restaurant, afterwards.

The 15th Annual Meeting will be on Tuesday 6 May 2014 in New York City.

Respectfully submitted,
Maria T. Lymberis, MD, HAPA Founder and Past President, and
Philip Candilis, MD, HAPA Secretary

8 May 2012 — Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

Note: this draft was approved by the HAPA Executive Committee, posted on the website, and ratified at the 14th Annual Meeting in May 2013 in San Francisco.

Members present: Drs. Katina Matthews-Ferrari, Maria Lymberis, Arthur Papas, Miltiades Zaphiropoulos, George Petrides, Philip Candilis. Guest: Bruce Hershfield.
During this meeting we also met Elias A. Iliadis, MD, President of the Hellenic Medical Society of Philadelphia, Konstantinos N. Tripodis, MD, psychiatrist from California, and Nikitas Moustakas, Esq., as the Hellenic Medical Society of Philadelphia held its annual meeting there.
Absent: Drs. Cassimatis, Christodoulou, Fouras, Vidalis, Papadimitriou, Zervas.

The minutes of the 12th Annual Meeting in Hawaii were distributed, reviewed and approved as written.

PRESIDENT'S REPORT

Dr. Matthews-Ferrari called the meeting to order at 6:00 PM. She noted that as President her primary focus remains membership and recruitment, as well as HAPA's IRS status. HAPA must wait a full year before a new tax ID can be assigned. Dr. Papas proposed that HAPA use the Massachusetts tax ID, but there was agreement to reject this as it would most likely only confuse the process at this point. HAPA's attorney believes HAPA should have its tax ID by spring 2013.

After HAPA's non-profit status is established, Katina and Maria will send a letter to community and academic leaders soliciting membership and financial support.

Recruitment efforts could include contacting a number of Greek-American organizations: the Hellenic Medical Association of New York, the Greek-American Behavioral Sciences Institute (GABSI), AHEPA, the Hellenic College in Boston, and local Greek Orthodox churches. As membership recruitment only works if there is recognisable value that potential members can appreciate, an old suggestion was made again — that HAPA consider offering talks at these venues and others where HAPA and its mission can be introduced. Arthur and Phil plan a Boston lunch for Greek and Greek-American colleagues to discuss local recruitment.

The potential membership of Thomas Mallios, a Manhattan psychologist and past president of GABSI, was discussed at length. The by-laws specifically include mental health professionals as Affiliate members. There was extensive discussion in support of full membership for psychologists but no action on revising the by-laws was taken. There was a strong objection to any psychologist having full or affiliate membership from Dr. Fouras (by email), but the majority was in full support of affiliate membership for psychologists as credentialed mental health professionals with philhellenic values, consistent with the needs of our organization and the interests of inclusivity. It was noted that for HAPA to maintain its APA Affiliate status it must fulfil the requirement that a majority of its members be APA members.

A motion was made by Dr. Papas and unanimously approved to invite Dr. Mallios to apply for HAPA Affiliate membership.

PRESIDENT-ELECT'S REPORT

Dr. Candilis noted that, given the difficult situation of HAPA while waiting for the tax ID, consideration should be given to maintaining the current officerships until full recruitment efforts can be made. He proposed to share the Treasurer's duties with Dr. Papas upon Dr. Fouras' resignation at the end of 2012; this was approved unanimously and the transition of banking to begin immediately. HAPA will maintain Wells Fargo as its bank and all dues cheques are to be mailed to the HAPA office address in California. Dr. Candilis will also contact Boston-area psychiatrists, AHEPA and the Dean of Hellenic College to explore their interest in HAPA.

TREASURER'S REPORT — Dr. Fouras was unable to attend; his report was presented. HAPA continues to run a deficit.

REPORTS FROM GREECE

Dr. Christodoulou emailed the latest programmes: the World Federation for Mental Health and the Hellenic Psychiatric Association are organising an international congress in Athens, 6–9 March 2013, on “Crises and Disasters: Psychosocial Consequences”, with the participation of the Psychiatric Association for Eastern Europe and the Balkans. The congress could provide an excellent opportunity to organise a HAPA meeting in Athens and link with the Greek psychiatric community; under present economic circumstances it is difficult for Greek colleagues to travel to the States, so the only way to come together is to participate in a major event in Greece.

Dr. Vidalis wrote: “In 2013 in Greece, despite the unbearable economic conditions, several significant psychiatric programmes are scheduled. One of them will be held on 21–23 February in Thessaloniki, entitled ‘The Cube of Psychiatry'. I would like to enthusiastically support the invitation of Dr. George Christodoulou for HAPA to participate in the upcoming World Federation for Mental Health Congress in Athens, as this promises to be an important scientific event not only for the Greek psychiatric community but also internationally. It would be a pity for HAPA to be absent.”

NOMINATIONS

The nominations approved at the 2011 meeting in Hawaii were unanimously confirmed: Councilor Arthur Papas until 2013; Dr. Zervas until 2015; Dr. Vidalis re-elected for a second term through 2016; Dr. Candilis to serve as President-Elect.

SCIENTIFIC PRESENTATION

“Physicians Caring for Physicians: Professionalism Among Us” — Philip J. Candilis, MD, DFAPA, Associate Professor of Psychiatry, Law and Psychiatry Program, University of Massachusetts Medical School.

Dr. Candilis spoke on his developing views of medical professionalism. He has written extensively on the ethics of the field and on what it means to be a psychiatrist, crafting a view of professionalism that integrates personal, professional and community values. This “robust” professionalism is exemplified in the work of state physician health programmes that assess, monitor and advocate for physicians having behavioural or health difficulties at work. He described the history of physician health programmes and some of the work at his own state's programme. With the increasing pressures on physicians to practise more quickly, cost-effectively and efficiently, such programmes are seeing increasing referrals and a renewed interest in exploring the standards that define medical professionalism.

ADJOURNMENT

Dr. Matthews-Ferrari closed the meeting at 8:15 PM. A group of members met for the Dutch-treat dinner at a local restaurant afterwards.

Respectfully submitted,
Philip Candilis, MD, HAPA Secretary, and
Maria T. Lymberis, MD, HAPA Founder and Past President

17 May 2011 — Honolulu, Hawaii

Note: this draft was approved by the HAPA Executive Committee, posted on the website, and ratified at the 13th Annual Meeting in May 2012 in Philadelphia.

Members present: Drs. Petrides, Kanellopoulou, Papastrat, Mavromatis, Dagadakis, Lymberis. Guest: Mrs Eleni Kanellopoulou.
Absent: Drs. Cassimatis, Candilis, Matthews-Ferrari, Christodoulou, Fouras, Vidalis.

Dr. Lymberis opened the meeting and welcomed all, noting that a number of officers were unable to attend. This meeting would have been chaired by incoming President Dr. Matthews-Ferrari, who had to cancel due to the death of her ailing father; the association sent its condolences to her and her family.

The minutes of the 11th Annual Meeting were distributed, reviewed and approved as written.

PRESIDENT'S REPORT — Dr. Lymberis read Dr. Cassimatis' message to the members.

TREASURER'S REPORT — Dr. Fouras was unable to attend; Dr. Lymberis presented his report. HAPA is running a deficit because of the lack of timely dues collection. A minimum of 20 full paying members is necessary for HAPA to stay in business. He urged everyone to take part in a membership drive.

THE FUTURE OF HAPA

Members present expressed their appreciation and affirmed the value of HAPA, but the recent problems of membership and poor attendance were noted again. There have been ongoing recruitment efforts over the last five or six years. Dr. Petrides noted that this is a very difficult time economically; Dr. Lymberis noted that all organizations have trouble with membership.

For several years now all HAPA business has been by email only. HAPA has never had any staff. Executive committee members have kept the organization alive by volunteering their services, personally contributing to fund its functions and lending funds to cover costs as needed. Dr. Lymberis has personally financed the website since 1999 and funded the recent upgrade, valued at $1,600.00; the Treasurer noted that this practice is not sustainable.

In 2010 it was discovered that HAPA had lost its legal status due to failure to register on a yearly basis. The decision was made to correct the problem by registering the organization and establishing a HAPA Foundation as a non-profit within the state of California. This required legal services at a cost of $2,400, funded by the executive committee members. A letter soliciting contributions was sent to all current and past members but the response was minimal; the request will be repeated with every dues request for the next few years.

Everyone present was urged to recruit at least one member before the 13th meeting in Philadelphia in 2012.

REPORTS FROM GREECE

Drs. Christodoulou, Vidalis, Zervas and other Greek psychiatrists are no longer able to travel as in the past, due to cutbacks in funding. Dr. Christodoulou invited HAPA members to the Hellenic Psychiatric Association's 21st Pan-Hellenic Congress, held in Athens 5–8 May; no one from HAPA was able to participate.

1) Professor George Christodoulou, 28 September 2011:

“I am back from the World Congress of Psychiatry in Buenos Aires — 15,000 participants. The Hellenic Psychiatric Association had the initiative to produce a book entitled ‘Anthology of Greek Psychiatric Texts', from the classical period up to the era of psychopharmacology in the 1950s. We decided to translate this book, insert three introductory articles by Christodoulou, Ploumpidis and Karavatos, and produce a WPA book. It took us three years to complete in English, but we thought it worth it, not only for scientific reasons but also for the upgrading of the damaged image of our country internationally. The production was funded by the Lilian Voudouri Foundation of Greece. We produced 10,000 copies, shipped them to Argentina and had them distributed free of charge to the participants of the World Congress. The Embassy of Greece and Ambassador Mr Michael Christides helped a great deal with the customs and by organising a reception, funded by the Hellenic Psychiatric Association, at the residence of the Ambassador. All the important people of international psychiatry were there. The reception of the book was enthusiastic.

Other news from Greece: on 10 October is World Mental Health Day. On this occasion the Hellenic Psychiatric Association, along with the World Federation for Mental Health and the two departments of psychiatry of the University of Athens, are organising a press conference on current pressing issues of mental health on 6 October, and the Hellenic Psychiatric Association is organising two round-table discussions at the psychiatric hospital at Daphni on 10 October. As you know, in periods of economic crisis psychopathology and especially suicide, which is closely associated with unemployment, increases. Additionally, mental health services are the first to suffer cuts internationally in such periods, and we want to prevent this if we can.”

2) Professor Athanasios A. Vidalis, MD, PhD, is President of the International Society of Quality Medicine, an international society of multiple medical specialties established in 2011 in Bulgaria. He has provided the leadership and inspiration for this group since 2002, when he helped initiate a series of World Congress meetings on “Quality in Clinical Practice” in Europe, and offered a warm welcome to any HAPA member wishing to join.

In his email of 24 August 2011 he wrote: “I also miss the USA. However, as you know, things have changed. The pharmaceutical companies have difficulties in supporting us in order to come to the HAPA conferences. I am sure it is not an uncommon problem, because American HAPA members did not have the chance to attend any meetings of the Pan-Hellenic Hospital Psychiatry Society either in Greece or abroad. I also share your worries about the difficulties in fostering the close collaboration of Greek and American psychiatrists. It is true that the USA and Greece are far away from each other, but I think it is not a problem we cannot solve. It would be great if we could find a chance to meet and discuss all these issues in person.”

NOMINATIONS

Dr. Petrides moved acceptance of the nomination of Dr. Zervas as candidate for the Councilor opening for 2011–2014. The motion passed unanimously.

SCIENTIFIC PRESENTATION

“Neuroprotection and Neurogenesis: The Added Promise of Psychotropic Medications” — Paul Barkopoulos, MD, MPH, Attending Medical Staff at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center, Los Angeles; Assistant Clinical Professor of Psychiatry at the UCLA Geffen School of Medicine.

Psychopharmacology clearly benefits patients by providing symptom reduction; however, there is no clear evidence that this treatment can modify the underlying disease process. There is clear evidence supporting the disease-modifying capacity of medications for multiple sclerosis, ALS, Parkinson's disease, epilepsy and possibly Alzheimer's — disorders considered neurological. For conditions considered psychiatric, such as schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, depression and PTSD, no disease-modifying therapy has been confirmed. This is perplexing, in that those psychiatric disorders are both neurological and psychiatric and share potential commonalities in their neurologic underpinnings, including deficits in neuroplasticity and glutamatergic dysfunction.

The talk reviewed the fundamentals of neurogenesis and neuroplasticity; contemporary understanding of alterations in neuroplasticity in bipolar illness, depression, PTSD and Alzheimer's disease; the evidence that various psychopharmacologic agents act in a neuroprotective fashion; and how this data lays a foundation for theories about the disease-modifying properties of currently used agents. It concluded with a potentially inspiring message for all psychiatrists: that not only are we capable of alleviating the symptoms of our patients, but we may become powerful agents in preventing, slowing or halting the progression of their illnesses.

ADJOURNMENT

Dr. Lymberis closed the meeting at 8:15 PM. A group of five members met for the Dutch-treat dinner at a local restaurant afterwards.

Respectfully submitted,
Maria T. Lymberis, MD
HAPA Founder and Past President

25 May 2010 — New Orleans, Louisiana

Note: this draft was approved by the HAPA Executive Committee, posted on the website, and ratified at the 12th Annual Meeting in May 2011 in Hawaii.

HAPA elections. The nominating committee presented the following nominations for the term 2011–2012:
President-Elect: Philip J. Candilis, MD
Treasurer: George Fouras, MD
Secretary: Philip J. Candilis, MD
Councilor for the term 2010–2013: Arthur N. Papas, MD

Members present: Drs. Cassimatis, Candilis, Kaliora, Matthews-Ferrari, Levounis, Lymberis, Petrides, Zaphiropoulos.
Unable to attend: Drs. Agallianos, Alexopoulos, Bouras, Cardasis, Christodoulou, Emmanouel, Kanellopoulou, Latoussakis, Lyketsos, Papas, Stratas, Papadimitriou, Papakostas, Zervas, Vidalis.
Invited guest: Bruce Hershfield, MD, APA Assembly Speaker.

(I) INTRODUCTIONS

HAPA President Dr. Cassimatis opened the meeting at 7:15 PM, welcoming all present and noting our special guest Dr. Hershfield. He thanked the members of the executive committee for their dedication, hard work and personal contributions, which have helped keep the organization going through these difficult times.

(II) PRESIDENT'S REPORT

Dr. Cassimatis asked for a moment of silence in memory of our founding member and past officer Michael Kalogerakis, MD, who died suddenly on 10 March 2010 while on holiday with his wife, Kay, in Florida. He was 83. Among his many accomplishments, he was Past President of the International Society for Adolescent Psychiatry and Psychology and a recipient of the American Society of Adolescent Psychiatry's Schonfeld Award.

He then announced several changes in the leadership following the resignations of the President-Elect and Treasurer. Dr. Matthews-Ferrari accepted appointment as President-Elect, Dr. Fouras as Treasurer and Dr. Candilis as Secretary, filling the last year of Dr. Matthews-Ferrari's term. All three are expected to be re-nominated at the 2011 Annual Meeting and elected to full three-year terms. Dr. Papadimitriou has finished his term as Councilor and a note of appreciation will be sent to him. Dr. Papas was nominated and elected as Councilor for 2010–2013.

(III) MINUTES

Dr. Lymberis presented the minutes of the 2009 tenth-anniversary meeting in San Francisco; approved as written.

(IV) TREASURER'S REPORT

In Dr. Papas' absence, Dr. Lymberis presented the financial report. During the first five or six years HAPA's yearly dues income was around $3,000 to $4,000, which covered the cost of the annual meeting. From 2006 there was a decrease in attendance with a corresponding decrease in dues.

Dues income 2007: $2,006.00 — annual meeting expenses $3,493.55
Dues income 2008: $525.55 — annual meeting expenses $2,693.70
Dues income 2009: $850.00 — annual meeting expenses $2,675.00

From 2007 HAPA began to run a deficit. Dr. Lymberis paid the cost of the dinners for 2008 and 2009. The executive committee urged each of its members to consider a contribution of $150.00, which was done from 2007; the deficits of 2007, 2008 and 2009 were covered by these contributions, and all bills were paid in full as of the end of 2009.

After 2008, as the global recession took hold, attendance and dues collection became an even bigger problem. In late 2009 the executive committee voted to change the format of the annual meetings, starting with this one: meetings continue on the Tuesday of the APA meeting but at 6:00–8:00 PM, with a Dutch-treat dinner at 8:30 PM at a local restaurant for those who wish to join. This year all members in attendance had a very successful, intimate and highly enjoyable dinner in a private room of the hotel restaurant, which helped with bonding as members got to know each other better. The success of this first meeting in the new format reassured everyone that it will serve all our future meetings well.

As of the 2010 meeting HAPA had no deficit: dues income 2010 $225.00, annual meeting expenses $122.17.

During 2010 HAPA also received a special contribution from Stella Lymberis, MD — $250.00 as seed money for the establishment of a fund “for a Greek American Scholarship Award in Psychiatry in memory of Styliani Orologa Lymberis, to be presented at a HAPA Annual Meeting to a deserving female resident for exceptional work during residency”. She and other family members will contribute to this fund over time.

Dr. Lymberis announced that she is funding the cost of $1,500.00 for the update of the HAPA website, already started and due for completion by the end of 2010.

(V) UPDATES FROM GREECE

A) From Professor Christodoulou, 25 April 2010:

“One of the main reasons that I will not be coming to New Orleans is that in the same month I have been invited by the WHO to give a course on ‘Advanced Psychiatry' to Palestinian physicians. I thought it was politically and substantially correct to accept this challenge and organise a course with the assistance of Prof. Yiannis Giouzepas, Prof. Dimitris Ploumpidis and Prof. Ilias Angelopoulos, who will accompany me to Palestine. The Hellenic Psychiatric Association will be the co-organiser with the WHO of this event.

You may remember that some years ago, when Lebanon and Israel were almost at war, a group of us visited Tel Aviv and Beirut and managed to persuade the two psychiatric associations to produce anti-war statements. The Palestinian Psychiatric Association received this initiative enthusiastically. It was carried out on behalf of the Institutional Programs on Disasters and on Violence of the WPA, but the Hellenic Psychiatric Association played a major role. On that occasion I remember Viveca Hashbun, a Palestinian child psychiatrist who took part in the Tel Aviv conference, saying that she was originally hesitant to come to a scientific meeting in Israel and that what made her decide was that the event was organised by the Greeks.

I mention these activities because they may give you ideas on how HAPA's activities may be shaped in the future. My opinion has always been that national politics is carried out more efficiently by NGOs than by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.”

B) From Professor Vidalis, 10 May 2010: due to many scientific and executive commitments in Greece he was unable to participate in the New Orleans meeting. He reported that “The Four Seasons of Psychiatry” meeting in Dubrovnik was a great success, sharing the comments of Professor P. Udomratn, Vice-Chairman of the Federation of Asian Psychiatrists: “The Four Seasons of Psychiatry is a meeting that I cannot find in any other place in the world. It expands the horizon of my knowledge of psychiatry to neuroradiology, neurology, nanomedicine, complex theory of mathematics, magnetoencephalography and more.”

(VI) SCIENTIFIC PROGRAMME

Petros Levounis, MD, MA, Director of the Addiction Institute of New York and Chief of the Division of Addiction Psychiatry at St. Luke's and Roosevelt Hospitals, and Associate Clinical Professor of Psychiatry at Columbia University College of Physicians and Surgeons, gave a scholarly and comprehensive presentation on his work with addictions. He noted that addiction is “the archetypal bio-psycho-social-brain disease”. Starting with a fascinating discussion of the history of addictions as illnesses, he moved on to the evidence base from twenty years of experience in treating them, and after focusing on the neurobiological, socio-cultural and treatment aspects, presented his main work on motivation and change — the subject of his then newly published book.

(VII) ADJOURNMENT

Dr. Cassimatis closed the meeting at 8:00 PM. The next Annual Meeting will be in Hawaii in May 2011.

Respectfully submitted,
Maria T. Lymberis, MD
HAPA Founder and Past President

Tuesday 19 May 2009 — San Francisco, California

Note: this draft was approved by the HAPA Executive Committee and ratified at the 11th Annual Meeting on 25 May 2010 in New Orleans.

Members present: Drs. Cassimatis, Cardasis, Markos Emmanouel, Katina Matthews-Ferrari, Fouras, Isabella Kanellopoulou, Lymberis, Papas, Petrides, Vidalis, Zaphiropoulos, with Mrs Stella Kaliora and Athena Papas.
Unable to attend: Drs. Georgopoulos, Stratas, Latoussakis, Alexopoulos, Agallianos, Christodoulou, Lyketsos, Kalogerakis, Papastrat, Papakostas and Zervas.
Invited guests: APA President Nada Stotland, MD, and Drs. Leah Dickstein and Carol Bernstein, who were able to come briefly. Professor J. K. Trivedi of India sent his regrets.

(1) INTRODUCTIONS

HAPA President Dr. Cassimatis opened the meeting at 7:10 PM, welcoming members, guests and our speaker Professor Nemeroff. He noted that this is his first meeting as President and that we are celebrating our organization's tenth birthday. HAPA is a small, all-volunteer organization but has made a considerable contribution by bridging the gap between Hellenic psychiatrists in the US and colleagues in Greece and the diaspora. This anniversary meeting was hoped to be very well attended, but the swine-flu scare coupled with recent global terrorist attacks made flying to the US problematic for many in Greece and elsewhere. He stressed that HAPA will continue through these hard times thanks to the committed work of the executive committee.

Dr. Cassimatis announced that he had accepted with regret the resignation, for personal reasons, of President-Elect Vassilios Latoussakis, MD, effective at the conclusion of this meeting. Dr. Latoussakis is a founding member who served in a leadership position with devotion and distinction and will continue as a member.

(2) MINUTES

Dr. Lymberis presented the minutes of the 2008 Annual Meeting; approved as written.

(3) TREASURER'S REPORT

Dr. Papas will submit his report for the 2008 and 2009 annual meeting expenses and dues income.

Dr. Lymberis noted that since 2002 HAPA has had no outside financial support. HAPA is a small APA Affiliate member organization entirely supported by member dues and by the generosity of members who make voluntary contributions. HAPA gratefully acknowledges the generous contributions of Drs. Nicolas Stratas and Katina Matthews-Ferrari, each of whom has contributed $500.00.

Since 2007 the cost of dinner meetings has increased dramatically because a minimum of 25 dinners is required for a dinner reservation. Since there is no way to predict that 25 or more members will attend, HAPA ends up paying the full cost of the reservation. Dues of $50.00 cannot cover our expenses. HAPA had a deficit in 2008, covered by a special contribution of $100.00 from each of the officers, and anticipates a deficit again in 2009.

All HAPA work is done by email; conference calls are at no cost to HAPA thanks to the generosity of our Presidents. Special thanks go to Drs. Petrides and Cassimatis, who personally arrange the monthly executive committee conference calls.

The annual dinner meeting is now the main expense. Publication of the HAPA Newsletter was discontinued in 2005 for lack of funding, and the offering of CME credits was discontinued because of cost. Given the deficits, the cost of the dinners will be re-evaluated.

Updating the HAPA website is an essential future project, since all HAPA correspondence is by email. The website was originally donated by Dr. Lymberis in 1999 at the time of the founding and now needs updating — hopefully by the 2010 Annual Meeting.

(4) UPDATES FROM GREECE

Professor Christodoulou, one of the founding members, was unable to attend but remains a very active member of the leadership and a crucial link with Greek and European psychiatric organizations and the WPA. He chaired the programme committee of the highly successful 20th Pan-Hellenic Psychiatric Congress in Crete, 14–18 May 2008, in which HAPA participated as co-sponsor; President Cassimatis and Drs. Petrides and Lymberis gave individual presentations and took part in the HAPA-sponsored panel on postgraduate psychiatric education in the US. He has organised the World Congress of Mental Health in Athens, 2–6 September 2009, and the Second Congress of Eastern Europe in Moscow, 27–30 October 2009; HAPA is a co-sponsor of both.

Dr. Vidalis, also a devoted founding member, is HAPA's link with psychiatrists in Thessaloniki and northern Greece and was the only HAPA member able to come from Greece this year. He is a distinguished leader in the Pan-Hellenic Hospital Psychiatry organization, organiser of many of its meetings and editor of its journal. This year's meeting takes place on Corfu in late May 2009; HAPA is a co-sponsor of that and of the annual “Seasons of Psychiatry” meetings.

At the 2008 meeting Dr. Vidalis had proposed the establishment of the office of HAPA Co-Chair or Vice-President from Greece, to help promote interest among Greek psychiatrists by providing a more direct leadership stake. It was pointed out that presently all three HAPA Councilors are from Greece and that all offices, including President-Elect, are open to all members including Greek psychiatrists. The Executive Committee reviewed the by-laws and drafted an amendment in consultation with Dr. Vidalis, presented at this meeting; given the absence of other members from Greece, the issue was tabled for a future meeting.

(5) SCIENTIFIC PROGRAMME

Dr. Papas introduced Charles B. Nemeroff, MD, Professor of Psychiatry at Emory, who gave a scholarly and detailed presentation on neuroscience and psychopharmacology under the title “Psychopharmacology in the 21st Century: Towards Personalized Medicine in Psychiatry”. An open, active discussion followed.

(6) ADJOURNMENT

Dr. Cassimatis thanked our speaker and all members for their participation and adjourned the meeting at 10:15 PM. The next Annual Meeting will take place in New Orleans in May 2010.

Respectfully submitted,
Maria T. Lymberis, MD
HAPA Founder and Past President

6 May 2008 — Washington, DC

Note: this draft was approved by the HAPA Executive Committee, posted on the website, and ratified at the 10th Annual Meeting in May 2009 in San Francisco.

Honorary guests present: Juan Enrique Mezzich, MD, President of the World Psychiatric Association; Roy Abraham Kallivayalil, MD, President of the Indian Association for Social Psychiatry and Professor and Head of the Department of Psychiatry, Medical College, Kottayam, India; George Bartzokis, MD, presenter.

Members present: Drs. Alexopoulos, Agallianos, Christodoulou (Immediate Past President, HPA) and Mrs Christodoulou, Cassimatis, Lymberis, Stratas, Latoussakis, Petrides, Papas and Mrs Papas, Papastrat.
Unable to attend: Drs. Lyketsos, Cardasis, Kalogerakis, Zaphiropoulos, Georgopoulos, Papakostas.

(1) INTRODUCTIONS

HAPA President Dr. Petrides opened the meeting at 7:10 PM. He noted that this is his last meeting as President, and that while our organization has reached the age of nine — a considerable achievement for a small, all-volunteer body — there is still much work to be done, primarily in membership recruitment and retention in the USA. He promised to continue to participate actively as Immediate Past President and thanked all members of the executive committee for their dedication and hard work.

(2) MINUTES

Dr. Lymberis presented the minutes of the 2007 Annual Meeting in San Diego, posted on the website with copies provided. Approved as written.

(3) TREASURER'S REPORT

Balance from 2006: $1,734.86
Dues income during 2007: $2,006.00
Expenses in 2007: $3,493.55
Dues collected in 2008: $525.00

Dr. Lymberis noted again that since 2002 HAPA has had no outside financial support and is entirely supported by member dues. For the second time this year the executive committee voted to charge for the cost of the dinner in addition to dues; the costs of meetings have gone up dramatically and dues of $50.00 are no longer sufficient. HAPA anticipates a deficit in 2009. Dues have remained unchanged since 1999, while the annual meeting now costs $2,000 to $3,000, without any staff or honoraria. All the work of HAPA is done by the officers by email and by conference calls at no cost to HAPA; our only costs are the annual meeting and the website.

(4) UPDATES ON PSYCHIATRY IN GREECE

Professor George Christodoulou, a vital supporter since the founding of HAPA, addressed the meeting. He is currently standing for President of the WPA. He is President of the Hellenic Centre for Mental Health and Research, Immediate Past President of the HPA, President of the Psychiatric Association for Eastern Europe and the Balkans, Chair of the WPA Committee on Ethics and Chair of the European Division of the Royal College of Psychiatrists.

He noted that the 20th Pan-Hellenic Psychiatric Congress in Crete, 14–18 May 2008, features several HAPA presenters and a panel on postgraduate psychiatric education with HAPA and HPA speakers. For 2009 he is organising the World Congress of Mental Health in Athens, 2–6 September, and the Second Congress of Eastern Europe in Moscow, 27–30 October.

Dr. Vidalis proposed the establishment of the office of HAPA Co-Chair for Greece. The proposal was accepted for consideration; the Executive Committee will review the by-laws and draft a proposal, in consultation with Dr. Vidalis, for discussion at the next Annual Meeting. Dr. Vidalis is also organising several meetings in Greece, including the General Hospital Psychiatry Conference in Corfu in May 2009 and four meetings in “The Four Seasons of Psychiatry” series.

(5) SCIENTIFIC PROGRAMME

Dr. Lymberis introduced George Bartzokis, MD, Professor of Neurology and Psychiatry at the UCLA Brain Research Institute, who presented “Brain aging and age-related risk factors for prevalent neurodegenerative disorders: implications for treatment and prevention”.

His talk focused on myelination, which has markedly expanded the timeline of what is considered normal human brain development. He discussed the unique process of human myelination and its role in producing the cortical environment that triggers Alzheimer's disease, and concluded with the impact of genetic and non-genetic risk factors on the age of onset.

In the lively discussion that followed he explained further: “Myelination of the cortex — necessary to become adults — sets up the necessary environment to develop the Alzheimer's pathology. As we get older the myelin breaks down. The actual pathology, plaques and tangles, develops as a result of the myelin breakdown and the continual repair attempts that follow. That is why Alzheimer's disease does not occur in ten-year-olds even when they have familial Alzheimer's disease genes — the myelination of the cortex must occur first. It is a permissive step. The myelin breakdown is what gives us the functional deficits, long before the pathology starts killing neurons.”

The presentation received very high marks for both content and delivery from all in attendance.

(6) ELECTIONS

Dr. Cassimatis, Chair of the Nominating Committee, presented the nominations for 2008–2011. After extensive discussion regarding the office of Secretary — Dr. Vidalis expressed his preference to continue as a Councilor — Katina Matthews-Ferrari, MD was nominated as Secretary and Athanasios Vidalis, MD as Councilor for another term. Both accepted and were unanimously elected, alongside President-Elect Vassilis Latoussakis, MD and Treasurer Arthur Papas, MD.

Dr. Petrides congratulated all and passed the office of President to Dr. Cassimatis, who thanked him for his service and outlined the goals of his presidency, stressing his determination to increase membership and improve HAPA's financial position.

(7) ADJOURNMENT

The meeting was adjourned at 10:10 PM. The next Annual Meeting will take place in San Francisco in May 2009.

Respectfully submitted,
Maria T. Lymberis, MD
HAPA Founder and Past President
