22 May 2007 — San Diego, California

Note: this draft was approved by the HAPA Executive Committee, posted on the website and ratified as written at the 9th Annual Meeting in May 2008 in Washington, DC.

Honorary guests present: Governor and Mrs Dukakis, Larry Tye, Konstantinos Roditis, Juan Enrique Mezzich MD (WPA President), Marcia Goin MD (Past APA President), Drew Clemens MD, Richard Shadoan and Mrs Shadoan, Thomas Ciesla MD (APA Trustee, Area VI).

Members present: Drs. Agallianos, Christodoulou (Immediate Past President, HPA) and Mrs Christodoulou, Cassimatis, Lymberis, Samolis, Gatos, Pantelis (Professor, Melbourne), Petrides, Roditis, Gross (SCPS President), Kader, Tsapakis, Locateli, Mariari, Galton, Kaliora, Vidalis, Mawhinney (President of the CPA) and Mrs Mawhinney, and Mrs Mary Thurrell (Past President of the APAA).
Unable to attend: Drs. Lyketsos, Cardasis, Kalogerakis, Kentros, Stratas, Kanellopoulou, Kachoris, Zaphiropoulos, Georgopoulos, Papakostas, Latoussakis, Papastrat.

(1) INTRODUCTIONS

HAPA President Dr. Petrides opened the meeting at 7:15 PM and welcomed members and honorary guests. He noted that this is an unusual occasion for two reasons: first, the honour of hearing at first hand the experience of a patient successfully treated with modern ECT; and especially, having such a prominent Greek-American family go public about psychiatric illness and its treatment. An abbreviated members' meeting was held to leave maximum time for the presenters.

(2) MINUTES

Dr. Lymberis presented the minutes of the 2006 Annual Meeting in Toronto, posted on the website with copies provided at the meeting. Approved as written.

(3) TREASURER'S REPORT

Balance from 2005: $4,110.30 (after expenses for the 2005 meeting)
Dues income during 2006: $1,523.59
Expenses in 2006: $3,899.03
Dues collected in 2006: $360.00
Balance as of 15 May 2007: $2,094.86

Dr. Lymberis noted that since 2002 HAPA has had no outside financial support and is now a member organization entirely supported by member dues. She urged everyone to become involved in recruiting new members, noting that HAPA's mission is vital in this world of interconnections and that it provides a valuable service by linking psychiatrists in the US with those in Greece and the rest of the world.

For the first time the executive committee asked members to pay an additional $15.00 to cover the cost of the dinner. Until now the annual dues of $50.00 have covered it; the dues have not been raised since our founding in 1999, while the costs of the annual meeting have gone up. HAPA has no paid staff and the work is done by the officers, mostly by email and through the website.

(4) UPDATES ON PSYCHIATRY IN GREECE

Dr. Christodoulou gave a comprehensive report on organized psychiatry in Greece. Under the umbrella of the World Psychiatric Association, the WPA Institutional Program on Disasters under his leadership, in collaboration with the Hellenic Psychiatric Association, was able to get the three national psychiatric associations of the three warring Middle East nations — Lebanon, Israel and Palestine — to independently produce a declaration against war. This is a small but impressive step in the right direction: psychiatry was able to bring all three to an agreement on the need to prevent the catastrophic personal and psychiatric damage the ongoing war inflicts on countless innocent civilians on all sides.

He noted excellent forthcoming meetings in Greece: the 20th Pan-Hellenic Psychiatric Congress in Crete, 14–18 May 2008; and, in 2009, the World Congress of Mental Health, sponsored by the World Federation of Mental Health, in Athens, 16–20 September 2009.

Dr. Vidalis and WPA President Dr. Mezzich also briefly addressed the meeting with news of their organizations and forthcoming meetings.

(5) SCIENTIFIC PROGRAMME

Dr. Petrides introduced three presenters. Mrs Kitty Dukakis spoke first, giving a very moving account of her personal battle with depression and how, finally and reluctantly, she agreed to ECT — a treatment that has changed her life. Governor Dukakis spoke second, giving the inside story of being the spouse witnessing the ravages of depression that were transforming his vibrant wife, and her dramatic return to her usual self with ECT. Larry Tye, co-author with Kitty Dukakis of the much-acclaimed book “Shock: The Healing Power of Electroconvulsive Therapy”, detailed his involvement in writing the book.

Dr. Petrides, who is closely involved in research on ECT and a member of the national multicentre CATE study, was the discussant. He presented the history, the stigma associated with this treatment modality, and the data as to its efficacy. An open discussion followed, with members actively interacting with the presenters.

(6) ADJOURNMENT

The meeting was adjourned at 10:00 PM. The next Annual Meeting will take place in Washington, DC in connection with the APA 2008 Annual Meeting.

Respectfully submitted,
Maria T. Lymberis, MD
HAPA Founder and Past President

23 May 2006 — Toronto, Canada

Note: these minutes were approved by the HAPA Executive Committee and ratified at the 8th HAPA Annual Meeting in May 2007 in San Diego.

Honorary guests: APA President Steven Sharfstein and WPA President Juan Enrique Mezzich.

Members present: Drs. Christodoulou, Latoussakis, Lymberis, Papakostas, Vidalis, Papastrat, Daskalakis, J. Giouzepas and C. Giouzepas, Papatriantaphyllou, Stathopoulou, Doxas, Pramateutakis, Askitis, Marmarokopou, Singelakis, Grigoriou, Papakostas, Athanasios Foussias and Agoritsa Foussias, Zaphiropoulos, Georgiopoulos, Gatos, Albright, Petrides, Karagon, Eliot Sorel.
Unable to attend: Drs. Kalogerakis, Kentros, Agallianos, Stratas, Cassimatis, Cardasis, Lyketsos, Besseghini, Kanellopoulou, Kachoris, Pantelis-Siotis, Gerothanasis.

(1) INTRODUCTIONS

HAPA President Dr. Petrides opened the meeting at 7:00 PM and welcomed everyone. He was very pleased to see so many members of the Hellenic Psychiatric Association attending and expressed his interest in promoting greater collaboration between the two organizations.

(2) HONORARY GUESTS

Dr. Sharfstein welcomed all to the APA Annual Meeting and expressed his appreciation for the invitation. He praised our efforts in fostering greater cooperation and communication between APA and HAPA members and members of the Hellenic Psychiatric Association. He had recently visited Greece for the 19th Pan-Hellenic Congress and praised the quality of the scientific sessions and Greek hospitality.

Dr. Mezzich spoke about the WPA's close relationship with the Hellenic Psychiatric Association. He has attended several Pan-Hellenic Psychiatric Congresses and expressed his appreciation for the Kos Declaration of 2004, which was endorsed by the WPA. He made a short presentation on the WPA's role in fighting mental illness.

(3) MINUTES

Dr. Lymberis presented the minutes of the 2005 Annual Meeting in Atlanta; approved as written with minor corrections.

(4) REPORT ON THE 19th PAN-HELLENIC CONGRESS

Dr. Lymberis reported on the just-concluded Athens congress — another highly successful meeting, and the 20th anniversary of the HPA, celebrated with an opening ceremony at the newly built Athens Concert Hall.

HAPA sponsored a special panel presentation chaired by Maria T. Lymberis, MD on ECT practice in Greece and the USA. President George Petrides, MD gave the main presentation on “The use of ECT for the treatment of acute major depression and relapse prevention: results from a multicentre trial by the CORE group”, followed by presentations from Ioannis Zervas, MD on “Cognitive disturbances in ECT: a review” and Ioannis Papakostas, MD on “Mechanism of ECT action”. The 90-minute session was attended by over 35 people who actively participated in the discussion.

The 19th Congress was the last organised under the leadership of Dr. Christodoulou, whose presidency of the HPA concluded with the election of Nikolaos Tzavaras, MD. HAPA will congratulate Professor Tzavaras and assure him of our continuing interest in maintaining the close relationship Dr. Christodoulou helped build over the last seven years. Dr. Christodoulou will remain active in HAPA in his capacity as Chair of the WPA Standing Committee on Ethics, President of the Hellenic Centre of Mental Health and Chair of the European Division of the Royal College of Psychiatrists.

(5) TREASURER'S AND MEMBERSHIP REPORT

Dr. Latoussakis noted that membership has not been growing as much as we need. Our annual meetings are now our only source of income, and are also our expense — postage, dinner and CME. We may face a deficit next year unless we gain more members or receive a generous tax-deductible contribution.

Income — balance as of August 2005 $4,110.30; dues received $1,523.59. Total $5,633.89.
Expenses — food, taxes and gratuity $3,145.20; audio-visual and taxes $753.83; CME and mailings $500.00. Total $4,399.03.
Balance as of August 2006: $1,234.86.

(6) BY-LAWS AMENDMENT PROPOSED

The By-Laws Committee submitted the following for consideration; members were invited to comment by email.

Problem: the current by-laws need to be amended to allow PhD psychologists to be full members of HAPA, provided they are members in good standing of the American Psychological Association or the corresponding professional organization of their own country. This change will not compromise HAPA's plans to apply to the APA Assembly for designation as an Allied organization, whose criteria are: a minimum of 100 members; 80 per cent or more of members being psychiatrists; and two-thirds of the psychiatrist members being members of the American Psychiatric Association.

Proposed amendment to Article III, Section 1 (Eligibility): members of the American Psychiatric Association, the American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, the Hellenic Psychiatric Association or comparable psychiatric associations in countries other than the United States will be eligible for membership. In addition, PhD psychologists who are members of the American Psychological Association, the Hellenic Psychological Association or a comparable association may be eligible upon the recommendation of the Membership Committee and approval by the Executive Committee, which must ensure that HAPA remains in compliance with the APA Assembly rules. No change to Section 2f (Affiliate Members).

Voting was deferred until there had been more time for comment and discussion.

(7) ELECTION OF COUNCILOR

Kanellos Charalambous, MD concluded his term as Councilor and was thanked for his work and support. Ioannis Papakostas, MD was unanimously nominated and accepted for 2006–2009.

(8) SCIENTIFIC PROGRAMME

The first presentation was by Ismene L. Petrakis, MD, Associate Professor of Psychiatry at Yale University School of Medicine, on “Advances in the treatment of alcohol dependence”. The lecture gave an overview of the use of medications in the treatment of alcohol dependence, beginning with the cultural history of alcohol from the Talmud and Old Testament through Plato and Hippocrates. In the US the lifetime prevalence is thought to be about 13 per cent and the twelve-month prevalence about 8 per cent of the general population; in Greece, rates of problematic consumption are thought to be lower, perhaps 2–6 per cent.

Three medications are approved in the US — disulfiram, naltrexone and acamprosate — all for uncomplicated alcoholism, while many patients are dually diagnosed and research is still needed for them. Dr. Petrakis presented three studies on dual diagnosis: a pilot study of naltrexone in patients with schizophrenia and alcohol dependence, in which those on naltrexone had fewer heavy drinking days and less craving; a national study of naltrexone utilisation in the VA system, which found a very low rate of use, associated with comorbid psychiatric disorders and recent hospitalisation; and a multi-site randomised trial of naltrexone, disulfiram or the combination in patients with comorbid Axis I disorders, in which those on active medication had a higher rate of consecutive days of abstinence than those on placebo, with no advantage to the combination.

She also discussed the period between early sampling of alcohol in adolescence and the transition to dependence by about age 25, particularly in individuals with a strong family history, and the use of pharmacologic probes to understand the underlying neurobiology of the glutamate and GABA systems. The implication is that alterations in these systems play a role in dependence and in vulnerability to it, and that treatments aimed at normalising them are an intriguing possibility for future research.

The second presentation was by George N. Christodoulou, MD, Professor of Psychiatry at the University of Athens, Immediate Past President of the Hellenic Psychiatric Association, Chair of the WPA Standing Committee on Ethics and President of the European Division of the Royal College of Psychiatrists, on “Ethics in psychiatry: from Hippocrates to the WPA Declaration on Ethics”. The presentation was very comprehensive and generated a great deal of interest.

(9) ADJOURNMENT

The meeting was adjourned at 10:30 PM. The next HAPA Annual Meeting will take place on 22 May 2007 in San Diego, California.

Respectfully submitted,
Maria T. Lymberis, MD
HAPA Founder and Past President

24 May 2005 — Atlanta, Georgia

Note: the draft of the 2005 minutes was approved by the HAPA Executive Committee and ratified at the 7th HAPA Annual Meeting in Toronto on 23 May 2006.

Members present: Drs. Lyketsos, Latoussakis, Lymberis, Papakostas, Vidalis, Georgiopoulos, Gatos, Rougas, Albright, Zachariadis, Kachoris, Petrides, Kentros, Karagon, Agallianos, Stratas, Papastrat, Tourlentes.
Unable to attend: Drs. Kalogerakis, Cassimatis, Zaphiropoulos, Cardasis.

(1) PRESIDENT'S REPORT

HAPA President Dr. Lyketsos opened the meeting at 7:00 PM. He noted that this is his last meeting as President and thanked all members of the executive committee for their help and support during his term of office.

(2) MINUTES

Dr. Lymberis presented the minutes of the 2004 Annual Meeting in New York; they were approved as written with minor corrections. The minutes of the 2004 First Joint HAPA–HPA Business Meeting in Kos were also presented and approved as written.

Dr. Lymberis noted that in 2006 the 19th Pan-Hellenic Psychiatric Congress will take place in Athens in May. She recommended that HAPA participate and plan for a second joint HAPA–HPA meeting.

(3) PRESIDENT-ELECT'S REPORT

Dr. Petrides noted that he was successful in obtaining CME credits for the HAPA scientific presentations, starting with the present meeting. Members expressed their appreciation for making the CME credits a reality.

(4) MEMBERSHIP

Dr. Lymberis reported the resignation of our long-time officer and Membership Chair, Dr. Cardasis, who has served with distinction since the founding of HAPA and will remain an active member. The resignation was accepted with gratitude and recognition for his service.

Dr. Lymberis proposed that, based on our experience over the last six years, the new Treasurer should also function as Membership Chair, allowing coordination of dues collection and membership.
ACTION: Approved unanimously.

(5) TREASURER'S REPORT

Dr. Latoussakis opened a new bank account for HAPA on the east coast with lower fees. His report:

Income — balance from the previous account $6,531.02; dues collected in 2005 $1,070.00. Total income $7,601.02.
Expenses — 2005 Annual Meeting (food and hotel) $2,241.72; meeting and secretarial costs $250.00; postage $250.00; audio-visual equipment $250.00; CME accreditation $500.00. Total expenses $3,491.72.
Balance as of August 2005: $4,109.30.

(6) HELLENIC PSYCHIATRIC ASSOCIATION REPORT

In March 2005 Dr. Christodoulou organised a very successful WPA congress in Athens — the first intersectional congress and also the first electronic congress in the history of the WPA. He is now organising the 19th Pan-Hellenic Congress of Psychiatry, scheduled for 4–8 May 2006 at the Athens Hilton, at which the 20th anniversary of the establishment of the Hellenic Psychiatric Association will be celebrated. He extended a warm welcome to all HAPA members.

Dr. Vidalis has been very active in northern Greece, developing the psychiatric community of Thessaloniki as another major centre for Greek psychiatry. He helped organise the 2nd World Congress on Quality in Clinical Practice in June 2004 in Porto Carras, Halkidiki, under the auspices of the Pan-Hellenic Society of General Hospital Psychiatry, which attracted over 450 participants. He is organising the 3rd World Congress on Quality in Clinical Practice for 28 September – 1 October 2006 in Thessaloniki, with over 1,000 participants expected.

The Pan-Hellenic Society of General Hospital Psychiatry has also organised a series of educational workshops on the theme “The Four Seasons of Psychiatry”. The first took place in September 2005 on Santorini; the second is scheduled for January 2006 in Kavala, focusing on the side effects of psychopharmacology, antipsychotic medication in the aged population, and new data in antipsychotic therapy. Its 3rd Pan-Hellenic Congress was held in January 2005 in Thessaloniki with more than 700 psychiatrists participating; the 4th is scheduled for spring 2007.

ACTION: It was voted unanimously that HAPA become a co-sponsor of the 4th Pan-Hellenic General Hospital Psychiatry Congress in 2007 in Thessaloniki. This co-sponsorship does not involve any financing from HAPA.

Dr. Vidalis urged members to send articles to the journal Hellenic Psychiatry of the General Hospital.

(7) ELECTION OF OFFICERS 2005–2008

President-Elect: Emmanuel Cassimatis, MD
Secretary: George Papakostas, MD
Treasurer: Vassilis Latoussakis, MD
Councilor: Athanasios Vidalis, MD

There were no further nominations from the floor. ACTION: accepted unanimously as submitted.

(8) SCIENTIFIC PROGRAMME

The first presentation was by HAPA member George I. Papakostas, MD, Assistant Professor of Psychiatry at Harvard Medical School and Clinical Assistant in Psychiatry at Massachusetts General Hospital, on “The role of folate in the treatment of depression”. Dr. Papakostas presented data from current research on the role of various folates, including SAMe, in the treatment of major depression. His research focuses on the pharmacotherapy of treatment-resistant major depressive disorder, including the role of individual symptoms, symptom clusters and syndromes, and on neuroendocrine and metabolic issues in MDD. He is the author or co-author of over 80 clinical and scientific publications and book chapters.

The second presentation was by Lisa Aronson, MSW, JD, PhD, Director of the Center for the Study of Mind and Human Interaction at the University of Virginia School of Medicine, on “Border Psychology: The Case of Cyprus”. Since 1974 there has been a de facto border in Cyprus between north and south, and there is a general preoccupation with that border which is contaminated by psychological factors. The presentation discussed how, under stressful conditions, physical borders take on psychological meanings: they become more than barriers separating territories — they become like a second skin that contains the large-group identity. When shared anxiety and its consequences occur, questions about borders and intrusions upon them become questions of identity. Ensuring the stability of physical borders may provide the necessary space and time to work through perceived threats to a group's identity without provoking violence and further conflict. The presentation drew on the Center's studies and on Dr. Vamik Volkan's pioneering work in large-group psychology.

(9) INTRODUCTION OF THE NEW PRESIDENT

Dr. Lyketsos thanked Dr. Petrides for his support and welcomed him as the next HAPA President. Dr. Petrides discussed his priorities: strengthening the organization, to which end he will initiate monthly executive committee conference calls on the last Monday of each month; and increasing membership — “We need to focus on the US HAPA members and reach out to psychiatrists of Greek origin here at home as well as in Greece.”

The meeting was adjourned at 10:30 PM.

Respectfully submitted,
Maria T. Lymberis, MD
HAPA Founder and Past President

Members present
From the HPA: Drs. Athanasios Vidalis, Iannis Zervas, Venos Mavreas, Yannis Papakostas, George Papadimitriou, Panagiotis Grigoriou, Stelios Stylianidis.
From HAPA: Drs. Constantine Lyketsos, Georgios Petrides, Maria Lymberis, Emmanuel Cassimatis.

Dr. Lyketsos chaired the meeting. There was enthusiastic agreement that HAPA is serving a real need in offering a formal connection for Greek and American psychiatrists. There was no formal agenda. Dr. Lymberis gave a brief history of the founding of HAPA and Dr. Lyketsos encouraged the participants to bring forth their concerns. An open, cordial and engaging discussion followed on: what HAPA can offer the HPA; what the needs and interests of Greek psychiatrists are; and how the HPA can help HAPA. This was the first time the HAPA leadership had the opportunity to hear directly from our colleagues in Greece.

1. EDUCATION

a) Visiting professorships — perhaps every October in Athens under the sponsorship of HAPA and the University of Athens. This would centre on an evening keynote lecture on a topic of broad interest to psychiatry but also of interest to physicians in all specialties. The visiting professor might also spend time with residents and faculty at the Aiginition Hospital on the days surrounding the keynote. Venos Mavreas will explore topics of interest among Greek psychiatrists through a series of focus groups in Greece and will be the contact person communicating the results to HAPA.

b) Education in the USA for Greek psychiatrists, residents and medical students going into psychiatry. Venos Mavreas will explore what types of education would be of value for different groups of doctors — health-system doctors, academics, fellows — with the idea of presenting a proposal to the ministry to support this in collaboration with HAPA.

c) Research support and mentorship, involving: review of papers before publication (HAPA will need a roster of members qualified and willing to do this, perhaps one or two papers a year in their area of expertise, commenting as a reviewer and suggesting a journal); help with the translation of scales and clinical measures into Greek; and the development of a seminar on clinical research methodology in psychiatry — perhaps a three- or four-day series with HAPA members as speakers in Greece, under HPA sponsorship at a Greek university.

2. CONSULTATION AND REFERRALS

There is a need for information about referrals in both directions, and a mechanism should be developed.

3. IMPROVING COMMUNICATIONS

· Write and provide a regular HAPA news column for Greek psychiatric publications.
· Greek HAPA members could write and provide a HAPA news page for posting on the message boards of all Greek hospitals with psychiatric residents.
· Greek HAPA members could help promote the HAPA Annual Meeting by finding out which Greek colleagues are coming to the APA meeting and sending a personal invitation. Fundraising could be attempted from pharmaceutical companies that support Greek psychiatrists' travel to the APA meeting.

Dr. Lyketsos will be coming to Greece with Dr. Alexopoulos in the autumn of 2004 for a conference. Both would be available to implement the idea of a HAPA–HPA visiting professorship, lecture at the university and meet with residents.

Respectfully submitted,
Maria T. Lymberis, MD — Clinical Professor of Psychiatry, UCLA; HAPA Founder and Past President
Constantine Lyketsos, MD — Professor of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences; HAPA President

body.en:
4 May 2004 — New York, NY

Note: this was a draft to be approved by the HAPA Executive Committee and ratified at the 6th HAPA Annual Meeting in New Orleans, May 2005.

HAPA President Constantine Lyketsos, MD was unable to attend. Dr. Lymberis, Founder and Past President, opened the meeting, welcomed everyone and asked President-Elect Dr. Petrides to chair. The meeting was called to order at 7:45 PM.

Members and guests present: Drs. Dennis and Georgia Agallianos, Manolis Cassimatis, Michael Kalogerakis, Socrates Pappas, George Alexopoulos, Nicholas Stratas, Miltiades Zaphiropoulos, Peter Lourgos, Stephanie Spanos, William Cardasis and Mrs Cardasis, George Christodoulou and Mrs Christodoulou, George Petrides, George Papadimitriou, Constantine Gatos, Dimitris Kiosses, Christina Demopoulos, Dimitra Hrisikos, Vassilis Latoussakis, Stella Lymberis, Mary Eugenia Theodorou, Lila Amirali and Maria Lymberis.

(I) PRESIDENT'S AND PRESIDENT-ELECT'S REPORTS

Dr. Petrides welcomed the members of the Hellenic Psychiatric Association — Drs. Kiosses, Gatos, Christodoulou — and our Councilor Dr. Papadimitriou. He noted that Secretary Dr. Zervas was unable to attend but would be present at the Kos meeting later that month.

(II) APPROVAL OF THE 2003 MINUTES

Dr. Lymberis noted that she is responsible for the minutes, which are posted on the website after approval of the draft by the Executive Committee and ratified at the next meeting. She requested that all members and guests review them and email any corrections or additions, preferably before the next meeting.

(III) TREASURER'S REPORT

Dr. Lymberis presented the report by Treasurer Dora Wang, MD, noting that Dr. Wang was present from the founding of HAPA and served as its first Treasurer with distinction. Dr. Wang submitted her resignation effective at the end of the year, as she is devoting her time to raising her daughter and working part-time.

In Dr. Wang's own words: “It has truly been a privilege and pleasure to have served as HAPA's Treasurer for the past four years. It is a credit to HAPA that you have welcomed me, whose ancestry is from such a northern outpost of Greece, into such an important role. Thanks to Georgia Agallianos for organising the mailing of dues notices this year — this has been a big help. HAPA is truly a spirited, visionary and all-encompassing organization, and I'm sure it will thrive for many, many long years. In the past two years I have taken on another kind of Hellenic American endeavour — I am trying to raise a Greek-American family, with influences from my own Asian Brazilian heritage. The position of HAPA Treasurer is one that I would recommend highly, as it is an opportunity to be a part of something that is truly important. Yassas!”

HAPA's income as of 30 April 2004:
Dues — general members $2,400; affiliate members $105; members in training $100; donation $35; interest $7. Total $2,647.
Expenses: $650. Net gain for the year: $1,997. Current balance: $7,776.07.

Dr. Lymberis noted that HAPA is in fair fiscal shape considering that we are still not well staffed and that all the work is done by members on a volunteer basis. She was again unable to obtain funding from any pharmaceutical company for the meeting and requested that members pay the full cost of the evening meal. Almost everyone present paid the full $80; several paid $100, and Dr. Stratas made a $500 contribution. Dr. Lymberis expressed her deep appreciation for the generous contributions, which indicate the shared commitment to a viable and growing HAPA.

She also discussed the change in the funding rules of the pharmaceutical industry: in future, CME credit will be needed for funding, which means our scientific programme has to be reviewed by the APA Annual Meeting Committee.

(IV) MEMBERSHIP REPORT

Dr. Cardasis reported 31 paid members before the APA meeting in New York, with further members expected to join at the meeting itself.

(V) HELLENIC PSYCHIATRIC ASSOCIATION REPORT

Dr. Christodoulou, as President of the HPA, informed participants of the plans for the 18th Pan-Hellenic Psychiatric Congress on the island of Kos, the birthplace of western medicine and home of Hippocrates. HAPA will participate in a number of ways: our President and Drs. Dunkas, Cassimatis and Lymberis will speak; there will be a jointly sponsored HPA–HAPA panel discussion under the title “A Win-Win Partnership for the Future”; and a members' meeting to discuss ways to strengthen the HPA–HAPA connection.

Dr. Christodoulou is leading the effort to organise the psychiatrists of Eastern Europe and the Balkans into an association under the WPA. He urged members to consider attending the Intersectional Congress of the WPA in March 2005 in Athens and the World Congress of Psychiatry in September 2005 in Cairo.

(VI) ELECTIONS

Dr. Charalambous was elected unanimously to a second term as Councilor, 2004–2007. Dr. Lymberis moved to accept, with regret, the resignation of Dr. Wang and nominated Dr. Georgia Agallianos to complete the remainder of her term as Treasurer; seconded and passed unanimously. Dr. Peter Lourgos, a new member in training, offered to work with Dr. Agallianos on the membership database.

(VII) SCIENTIFIC PRESENTATION

Dr. Petrides closed the members' meeting at 9:00 PM and introduced Dr. Alexopoulos, who presented “What can cognitive impairment teach us about depression?” — an excellent presentation of cutting-edge research that provoked a stimulating discussion. The meeting closed at 10:30 PM.

The Sixth HAPA Annual Meeting will take place in New Orleans in May 2005.

Respectfully submitted,
Maria T. Lymberis, MD
HAPA Founder and Past President

body.en:
20 May 2003 — San Francisco, California

These minutes were approved by the HAPA Executive Committee. Final ratification at the HAPA 2004 meeting.

HAPA President Dr. Lyketsos called the meeting to order at 7:15 PM.
Members present: Drs. Agallianos and Georgia Agallianos, Cassimatis, Wang, Tsopelas, Petrides, Vidalis, Charalambous, McDevitt, Zaphiropoulos, Lyketsos.

(I) PRESIDENT'S REPORT

Dr. Lyketsos noted that HAPA has been making significant connections with the Hellenic Psychiatric Association in Greece. He has made several scientific presentations and Dr. Lymberis, as Founder, presented at the 17th Pan-Hellenic Psychiatric Congress in 2002. He noted that fear of SARS and the after-effects of the Iraq war and 11 September have resulted in fewer Greek psychiatrists travelling to the US for the APA meeting this year. He welcomed Dr. Vidalis, who has faithfully attended HAPA's annual meetings for the last three years.

Dr. Lyketsos gave special thanks to Dr. Cardasis, Chair of the Membership Committee, and to Dr. Wang, whose work as Treasurer has been essential to the vitality of HAPA. He noted that Dr. Lymberis has continued to work for HAPA and is responsible for setting up and publicising our annual meetings, preparing the minutes, and working on our website and newsletter. In recognition of her vision in founding HAPA and her continued efforts, Dr. Lyketsos moved that HAPA ask the HPA to honour Dr. Lymberis at the upcoming 18th Pan-Hellenic Psychiatric Congress in Kos, 14–17 May 2004.

MOTION: HAPA recommends that Dr. Lymberis' contributions to HAPA as founder and past president be recognised with an award. Carried unanimously.

Dr. Lyketsos presented a proposal for establishing a HAPA Educational Fund to be used for postgraduate training by Greek psychiatrists in recognised US academic centres. As a pilot programme he will personally solicit funds from private donors and pharmaceutical companies in order to fund a Greek psychiatrist for three to six months, up to a year, to work under his mentorship at Johns Hopkins. If successful, other HAPA members will be identified as mentors able to sponsor a Greek psychiatrist at their institutions.

HAPA EDUCATIONAL FUND — SUPPORT OF HELLENIC SCHOLARS

Aim: to provide financial support for a targeted, post-residency educational experience for Greek psychiatrists in academic institutions in the United States.

Mentors: HAPA will survey its members to create a database of academic mentors willing and able to sponsor a Greek psychiatrist to spend three to six months in the USA undergoing post-residency education. The database will contain the name and institution of the sponsor and the areas in which education might be provided, and will be updated annually.

Fundraising: funds may be raised from foundations, private donations, the pharmaceutical industry, or from individual HAPA members, and will be maintained in a separate account. Ten per cent of funds raised will be retained by HAPA to offset administrative expenses. The first target is one grant per year of $5,000 to a selected scholar, who may use the funds for travel, lodging and other reasonable expenses. An additional $1,000 will be provided to the sponsoring mentor and institution. The grant is not intended to cover the full expenses of the experience, but to help defray some of the costs; scholars will supplement it from other sources.

Selection: the HAPA Educational Fund Committee, appointed ad hoc by the President and co-chaired by the President and Immediate Past President, will administer the programme and select the scholars. It will issue a request for applications to the academic departments of psychiatry and relevant professional associations in Greece, also published on the website and in the newsletter along with the list of available mentors.

Submissions will contain: (1) a letter from the nominating individual or institution specifying the reasons for the nomination, the qualifications of the nominee and the scientific and educational merits of the proposed experience; (2) a letter from the proposed scholar specifying the aims of the experience and its relationship to their career goals, with proposed dates and supplementary funding sources; (3) the nominee's curriculum vitae.

Release of funds: upon receipt of a letter from the mentor confirming arrangements, HAPA will issue cheques for half the grant to the scholar and the US institution; the remainder on confirmation of the scholar's arrival.

Final report: within one month of completion, the scholar and mentor will provide HAPA with a report of two to three pages detailing the outcome, to be summarised on the website and in the newsletter.

Membership: HAPA scholars receive one year's free membership during the year of their educational experience.

MOTION: To authorise Dr. Lyketsos to move forward with solicitation of funds for the HAPA Educational Fund and to establish an ad hoc committee, chaired by Dr. Lyketsos with Drs. Petrides, Cassimatis and Lymberis, to screen candidates for the 2003–2004 project at Johns Hopkins. Seconded and approved unanimously.

Dr. Lyketsos announced that HAPA will be an official co-sponsor of the 2004 HPA meeting.

MOTION: To hold the Fifth HAPA Annual Meeting on Tuesday, 4 May 2004 in connection with the APA Annual Meeting in New York City. Seconded and passed unanimously.

(II) PRESIDENT-ELECT'S REPORT

Dr. Petrides expressed his appreciation for the hard work of the officers and committee chairs. He is excited by the opportunity to chair the HAPA Scientific Program Committee for the 2004 New York meeting and will ensure it is well publicised to residents in New York area hospitals. He will also work closely with Dr. Lyketsos in the selection of mentors for the Educational Fund and in publicising HAPA's programmes in the New York area Greek media. He expressed concern about membership recruitment and expansion.

(III) TREASURER'S REPORT

Dr. Wang presented the annual status of HAPA. From May 2002 through 30 April 2003, HAPA collected $1,970 in dues; total income for the period was $2,016.76, which included a donation by Dr and Mrs Agallianos. Expenses for the same period were $6,790.93, leaving a balance of $4,465.07 as of 30 April 2003. She stressed the need for a more intense dues-collection effort, and thanked Dr. Lymberis for obtaining a grant from Janssen Pharmaceutica that covered the expenses of the 2003 meeting.

(IV) REPORT BY DR. VIDALIS

Dr. Vidalis expressed his appreciation for HAPA's efforts in providing opportunities for Greek psychiatrists and reported on the activities of Greek psychiatrists in Northern Greece, including the launching of the World Congress on Quality of Life and of a new scientific journal on hospital psychiatry. He reported that the 2nd Pan-Hellenic Congress of Psychiatry in the General Hospital was held in Thessaloniki, 7–9 February 2003, on the theme “The Clinical Approach of Psychiatry”, with 75 presentations and very good attendance.

(V) REPORT BY DR. LYMBERIS

Dr. Lymberis thanked Janssen Pharmaceutica for funding HAPA's Fourth Annual Meeting. Work on the website is continuing and another membership drive is planned for the autumn. Dr. Cardasis reported that over 160 members have paid dues in the last four years, but not all renew. Dr. Lymberis proposed that the upcoming membership drive include a telephone tree by the officers and members, as a personal connection should help increase membership.

She also reported on the Boston HAPA chapter's request for HAPA to sponsor their local scientific meeting of 2 May 2003, devoted to “Mental Health Services, Practices and Plans in Greece”, with Dr. Stelios Stylianidis, Medical Director of the Child Psychiatric Hospital of Attica, as speaker. Their programme was a great success and this event can be repeated in other areas; HAPA charges an administrative fee of ten per cent for such co-sponsoring.

(VI) NOMINATING COMMITTEE

Dr. Charalambous was unanimously elected to a second term as Councilor, 2003–2006.

(VII) NEW BUSINESS

Dr. Kalogerakis raised concerns about a wave of anti-Americanism he encountered on a recent trip to Greece and asked whether there were psychiatric aspects HAPA could address. A lively discussion followed. It was felt that, while disturbing, the phenomenon is not a psychiatric issue for HAPA to address.

(VIII) SCIENTIFIC PRESENTATION

Dr. Lyketsos presented “Neuropsychiatric Disturbances in Alzheimer's Disease”, detailing the results of his ten years of research in the area. The presentation was enthusiastically received and generated a great deal of interest.

The meeting concluded at 10:10 PM.

Respectfully submitted,
Maria T. Lymberis, MD
HAPA Founder and Immediate Past President

21 May 2002 — Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

Members present: Drs. Lymberis, Lyketsos, Christodoulou, Zaphiropoulos, Petrides, Agallianos, Dunkas, Mavromatis, Togias, Pandelidis, Papadimitriou, Papakostas, Papastrat, Sambunaris, Spanos, Vidalis, Syngelakis, Oikonomou, Latoussakis, Tzevelikos.

The meeting was called to order at 7:00 PM by Maria T. Lymberis, MD, HAPA President, who welcomed everyone, especially our members from Greece and the President of the Hellenic Psychiatric Association and his wife, Dr and Mrs Christodoulou.

(1) MINUTES OF THE SECOND ANNUAL MEETING

Dr. Lymberis noted that the minutes of the 2001 HAPA meeting are in the January 2002 issue. Upon their approval today, these minutes will also be published in the HAPA Newsletter and on the website.
ACTION: The motion to approve the minutes was moved and seconded. The minutes were approved as written.

(2) PRESIDENT'S REPORT

Dr. Lymberis noted that the HAPA Newsletter was issued in January 2002 due to numerous unexpected problems, including the tragedy of 11 September 2001. It is hoped that there will be another HAPA Newsletter prior to the 2003 Annual Meeting. She urged everyone to consider items for submission. She suggested that an annual report from the Hellenic Psychiatric Association should be a regular feature of our newsletter, and urged our HAPA members from Greece to submit such a report for the next issue.

(3) TREASURER'S REPORT

Our Treasurer was unable to be present but submitted her written report, dated 21 May 2002, stating HAPA's financial condition from 1 May 2001 through 30 April 2002:

Income: $7,035.95
Expenses: $3,195.50
Balance as of 30 April 2002: $11,091.24

It was noted that Dr. Lymberis was unable to obtain any financial support for HAPA for our 2002 meeting. She urged that HAPA members and officers help in the effort to obtain educational funding for our meetings from pharmaceutical companies for 2003.

(4) MEMBERSHIP COMMITTEE

Membership Chair Dr. Cardasis noted that he has a full record of HAPA members and has been working closely with our Treasurer, Dr. Wang, to keep the lists current. Dr. Lymberis will obtain from the APA the names of all Greek-speaking APA members for our 2002–2003 membership drive. Dr. Cardasis reported that HAPA membership is close to 100 members, but not all members renew annually. The dues letter is sent annually by the President in the late summer or early autumn; most members pay at the Annual Meeting. We must all make every effort to increase our membership.

(5) HAPA WEBSITE

Dr. Lymberis noted that the website needs updating and submitted an estimate of $3,000 from our current host.
ACTION: Moved, seconded and approved unanimously.

(6) REPORT ON THE 17th PAN-HELLENIC CONGRESS, HALKIDIKI

Dr. Lymberis attended the 17th Pan-Hellenic Psychiatric Congress of April 2002 as HAPA President and Founder. She reported that she was greatly impressed with the scientific content of the meeting and the enthusiasm and commitment of Greek psychiatrists to patient care. She strongly urged that HAPA actively promote the upcoming 18th Pan-Hellenic Psychiatric Congress of 2004.

(7) REPORT OF THE PRESIDENT OF THE HELLENIC PSYCHIATRIC ASSOCIATION

Dr. Christodoulou expressed his appreciation for HAPA's continued support and reported on a number of scientific activities and projects being pursued in Greece and abroad. He and a number of HPA members are also very active in the World Psychiatric Association. He emphasised his appreciation for HAPA's interest in participating in the Pan-Hellenic Psychiatric Congress.

(8) INSTALLATION OF THE NEW PRESIDENT

Dr. Lymberis expressed her deep gratitude to the members of the original HAPA Steering Committee for helping make the dream of establishing HAPA come true, and especially thanked Dr. Christodoulou for his enthusiastic support. She noted that, as her term of office comes to a close, HAPA at three years old has proven to be a solid bridge for our fellow psychiatrists in Greece and throughout the Greek diaspora. At our scientific meetings we have had presentations from distinguished Greek psychiatrists from Greece, Australia, England and the US. We are attracting young psychiatrists in training as members; they provide vitality and represent the future leaders of our profession. HAPA is off on a solid footing and growing. She emphasised that none of this would have been possible without the commitment of the HAPA officers and committee members.

Dr. Lymberis introduced Dr. Lyketsos as the next HAPA President, his term starting at the conclusion of the 2002 Annual Meeting. She expressed her appreciation for his support in the early efforts to establish HAPA. His assuming the presidency means that “HAPA is here to stay and it is making roots”.

Dr. Lyketsos expressed his appreciation to Dr. Lymberis for her vision in establishing and maintaining HAPA: “Dr. Lymberis is the soul of HAPA. She has single-handedly run the organization to date, doing the lion's share of the work with the able support and help from our officers, especially Drs. Wang and Cardasis.” He noted that, due to unexpected professional demands, he had seriously considered not going through with the presidency, but Dr. Lymberis graciously and emphatically assured him of her continued presence, support and active involvement: “HAPA has to move forward. You must take office as its next President and I will do all I can to help.”

Dr. Lyketsos then outlined his goals for HAPA:
· expanding the membership to 100 members so HAPA can become officially an Affiliate psychiatric organization in the APA Assembly;
· co-sponsoring with the HPA the 18th Pan-Hellenic Psychiatric Congress in the birthplace of the father of medicine, Hippocrates, on the island of Kos in 2004;
· holding HAPA's 2004 Annual Meeting in Kos, Greece rather than in the United States.

(9) NOMINATING COMMITTEE AND ELECTIONS

After considerable discussion, the following were moved, seconded and approved unanimously for 2002–2005:

President-Elect: George Petrides, M.D.
Secretary: Yannis Zervas, M.D.
Treasurer: Dora Wang, M.D.
Councilors: Kanellos Charalambous, M.D. (2000–2003); William Cardasis, M.D. (2001–2004); George Papadimitriou, M.D. (2002–2005)

(10) NEW BUSINESS

The Fourth Annual HAPA Meeting will be on Tuesday, 20 May 2003 in San Francisco in association with the APA Annual Meeting.

(11) SCIENTIFIC PROGRAMME

Dr. Lymberis presented on the psychiatric aspects of traumatisation from acts of terrorism and torture. She noted that both the APA and the World Psychiatric Association have declared a strong commitment to addressing these issues, and that in the United States psychiatric interest in treating victims of political torture is strong and has a long history. The events of 11 September 2001 shook the widely shared view of the USA as a safe haven. Psychiatrists, along with all types of mental health professionals, made a major effort and provided acute treatment, consultation and counsel to organizations and people affected by this tragedy. Issues of PTSD and its treatment became real and acceptable, which helped greatly in the fight against the stigma associated with our field.

The presentation included an edited version of “Your Neighbours' Son”, a 65-minute film made by Amnesty International in Denmark in 1982, about the training of conscripts at KESA, the Greek military police training centre during the years of the dictatorship. The film has direct interviews and testimony from former conscripts and torture victims, and reconstructs the process whereby normal young Greek men were systematically transformed into torturers. It also deals with the effects of the torture on victims and on the torturers.

An extensive and lively discussion followed. It was an intensely emotional experience for all present. Dr. Christodoulou stressed the psychiatric work of the WPA and focused on the political aspects of this intensely political period of Greek history. Dr. Lymberis closed the meeting, emphasising that, as psychiatrists, we are all called upon to study and understand all aspects of human experience, including those which elicit powerful reactions in us.

The meeting was closed at 10:15 PM.

Respectfully submitted,
Maria T. Lymberis, MD
HAPA Founder and Past President

body.en:
May 8, 2001 — New Orleans, Louisiana

The meeting was called to order at 8 p.m. by HAPA Founding President, Maria T. Lymberis, MD.

Dr. Lymberis welcomed everyone and noted that the change of time — from early on Saturday for lunch during the APA Annual Meeting to later on Tuesday for dinner — had resulted in a much larger number of Greek psychiatrists in attendance. This was significant because part of HAPA's mission is to develop a close relationship with our Greek colleagues, and the presence of so many Greek psychiatrists during this meeting was noted as a significant step in HAPA's growth.

Dr. Lymberis urged everyone to work on the HAPA Membership Drive. “Pass the word about HAPA's value. This is YOUR organization!” HAPA's goal is to reach at least 100 members so it can be included formally in the APA Assembly as an Allied Professional Organization. Dr. Lymberis noted that all of the HAPA officers have been working very hard this year: “We are beginning to have a real organizational structure with results to be proud of.” Specifically, the HAPA Membership Chair, Dr. Cardasis, has been developing our membership list which will be posted on our website in the near future. HAPA Treasurer, Dr. Wang, has moved the HAPA bank account to get better service, while taking care of IRS requirements. She noted that our balance as of 7 May 2000 was $9,839.17. Dr. Lymberis expressed regret that HAPA Secretary Dr. Alexopoulos was unable to attend due to travel problems, and again kept the minutes.

Dr. Lymberis expressed HAPA's appreciation for the sustained support that AstraZeneca has given HAPA. It has provided HAPA with an educational grant every year, starting with our founding in 1999. With this support, HAPA has been able to grow and provide our members with the HAPA Newsletter, website and, most importantly, our scientific programmes.

HAPA President-Elect Constantine Lyketsos, MD also welcomed everyone and noted his commitment to increasing HAPA's visibility and participation in psychiatric scientific meetings in Greece. He also emphasised the need for HAPA to launch an outreach membership programme in England and Australia, where large numbers of psychiatrists of Greek origin are found. He noted that our presenters at this meeting are from these countries and hoped that both would support this effort.

Hellenic Psychiatric Association President George Christodoulou, MD expressed his appreciation for the work of HAPA, thanking Dr. Lymberis for her efforts in making HAPA possible. He gave a brief update of psychiatric developments in Greece.

The President of the Hellenic Society of Psychoanalytic Psychotherapy, Grigoris Vaslamatzis, M.D., was unable to attend our meeting, but he had invited HAPA to their very successful meeting of November 2000 in Athens. Dr. Lymberis had sent a letter expressing HAPA's interest in continuing to collaborate in fostering scientific exchange with our Greek colleagues.

Minutes of the First Annual HAPA Meeting of 15 May 2000 were approved as written. HAPA Membership Committee Chair William Cardasis, MD reported on the status of the HAPA membership. HAPA Treasurer Dora Wang, MD reported on the status of HAPA's finances and noted that the budget for 2002 will be presented to the executive committee for approval by November 2001. Nominating Committee Chair Maria Lymberis, MD reported on the committee's recommendation to re-elect William Cardasis for HAPA Councilor for another three-year term, 2001–2005.

HAPA Scientific Program Chair Constantine Lyketsos then opened the scientific programme, which presented cutting-edge research by two outstanding Greek psychiatrists from Greece and Australia. The first, Christos Pantelis, MD, Associate Professor and Head of the Cognitive Neuropsychiatry Research and Academic Unit at the University of Melbourne & Mental Health Research Institute, spoke on “Structural Neuroimaging and Neuropsychological Findings in Schizophrenia: From Prodrome to Established Schizophrenia”. The second speaker, Nick Stefanis, MD, Lecturer in the Department of Psychiatry at the University of Athens, presented “Prodromal Features to Schizophrenia: A Study of Greek Military Recruits”.

The meeting adjourned at 10:15 pm with the promise of another successful HAPA meeting in Philadelphia in May 2002.

Respectfully submitted,
Maria T. Lymberis, M.D.
body.el:
8 Μαΐου 2001 — Νέα Ορλεάνη, Λουιζιάνα

Η συνάντηση κηρύχθηκε σε έναρξη στις 8 μ.μ. από την ιδρύτρια Πρόεδρο της HAPA, Maria T. Lymberis, MD.

Η Dr Lymberis καλωσόρισε τους παρευρισκόμενους και σημείωσε ότι η αλλαγή της ώρας — από γεύμα νωρίς το Σάββατο σε δείπνο την Τρίτη κατά τη διάρκεια της Ετήσιας Συνάντησης της APA — είχε ως αποτέλεσμα πολύ μεγαλύτερη συμμετοχή Ελλήνων ψυχιάτρων. Αυτό ήταν σημαντικό, καθώς μέρος της αποστολής της HAPA είναι η ανάπτυξη στενής σχέσης με τους Έλληνες συναδέλφους.

Η Dr Lymberis προέτρεψε όλους να εργαστούν για την προσέλκυση μελών: «Διαδώστε την αξία της HAPA. Αυτή είναι η δική ΣΑΣ εταιρεία!» Στόχος είναι τα 100 μέλη, ώστε η HAPA να ενταχθεί επίσημα στη Συνέλευση της APA ως συνεργαζόμενος επαγγελματικός φορέας. Σημείωσε ότι όλα τα μέλη του συμβουλίου εργάστηκαν πολύ σκληρά: «Αρχίζουμε να έχουμε πραγματική οργανωτική δομή με αποτελέσματα για τα οποία μπορούμε να είμαστε περήφανοι.» Ο Πρόεδρος της Επιτροπής Μελών, Dr Cardasis, καταρτίζει τον κατάλογο μελών που θα αναρτηθεί σύντομα στην ιστοσελίδα. Η Ταμίας, Dr Wang, μετέφερε τον τραπεζικό λογαριασμό για καλύτερη εξυπηρέτηση· το υπόλοιπο στις 7 Μαΐου 2000 ήταν 9.839,17 δολάρια.

Η Dr Lymberis εξέφρασε την εκτίμηση της HAPA για τη συνεχή στήριξη της AstraZeneca, η οποία προσφέρει εκπαιδευτική επιχορήγηση κάθε χρόνο από την ίδρυση το 1999. Χάρη σε αυτήν η HAPA μπόρεσε να αναπτυχθεί και να προσφέρει στα μέλη της το ενημερωτικό δελτίο, την ιστοσελίδα και, κυρίως, τα επιστημονικά της προγράμματα.

Ο Εκλεγμένος Πρόεδρος Constantine Lyketsos, MD, δεσμεύτηκε για αύξηση της παρουσίας της HAPA σε ψυχιατρικά επιστημονικά συνέδρια στην Ελλάδα και τόνισε την ανάγκη προσέγγισης μελών στην Αγγλία και την Αυστραλία, όπου υπάρχουν πολλοί ψυχίατροι ελληνικής καταγωγής.

Ο Πρόεδρος της Ελληνικής Ψυχιατρικής Εταιρείας, George Christodoulou, MD, εξέφρασε την εκτίμησή του για το έργο της HAPA και ενημέρωσε συνοπτικά για τις εξελίξεις στην ψυχιατρική στην Ελλάδα.

Τα πρακτικά της 1ης Ετήσιας Συνάντησης εγκρίθηκαν ως είχαν. Ακολούθησαν οι εκθέσεις της Επιτροπής Μελών και του Ταμείου· ο προϋπολογισμός του 2002 θα υποβαλλόταν προς έγκριση έως τον Νοέμβριο του 2001. Η Επιτροπή Υποψηφιοτήτων εισηγήθηκε την επανεκλογή του William Cardasis ως Συμβούλου για νέα τριετία, 2001–2005.

Στο επιστημονικό πρόγραμμα παρουσιάστηκε πρωτοποριακή έρευνα από δύο εξέχοντες Έλληνες ψυχιάτρους: ο Christos Pantelis, MD, από το Πανεπιστήμιο της Μελβούρνης, με θέμα «Δομική νευροαπεικόνιση και νευροψυχολογικά ευρήματα στη σχιζοφρένεια», και ο Νίκος Στεφανής, MD, από το Πανεπιστήμιο Αθηνών, με θέμα «Πρόδρομα χαρακτηριστικά της σχιζοφρένειας: μελέτη σε Έλληνες νεοσύλλεκτους».

Η συνάντηση έληξε στις 10:15 μ.μ.

Με εκτίμηση,
Maria T. Lymberis, M.D.

body.en:
May 15, 2000 — Chicago, Illinois

The meeting was called to order at 12:30 p.m. by Maria T. Lymberis, MD, HAPA President, who welcomed members and guests.

I. The minutes of the HAPA Inaugural Meeting of October 1999 were approved as noted in the HAPA Newsletter and website, with the following correction: Linda Kalivas was present at the 1999 meeting.

II. PRESIDENT'S REPORT

Dr. Lymberis expressed her appreciation for AstraZeneca's support of our scientific meetings for the second year. We are still a very young organization with very limited resources and great plans. The year has been spent developing our basic structures with very little outside funding and a small membership dues base. We did it by doing the work “at home”. Specifically, HAPA was able to keep costs down by getting the vital work of HAPA done by members of her family. She thanked her son Anthony De Cordoba who donated his time and expertise to HAPA by designing the logo and the website. The website was launched in April 2000 by her son's company, Vista View Imagery Ltd., which is hosting the HAPA website free of charge for the next three years. Finally, Dr. Lymberis thanked her husband, Pedro De Cordoba, for his invaluable help with HAPA membership, banking, billing and mailings through his office. Next year some of these functions are expected to be done by several HAPA officers.

Dr. Lymberis announced several very important meetings to be held in Greece this year: the Fifth Delphi International Psychoanalytic Symposium, “Self Knowledge: Before and After Freud”, in Delphi, 25–30 July 2000; the Second International Congress “Hormones, Brain and Neuropsychopharmacology” in Rhodes, 15–19 July 2000; and the 11th Conference of the Hellenic Society for Psychoanalytic Psychotherapy in Athens, 23–26 November 2000.

Dr. Lymberis reported that she had received a letter from the psychiatrist Kirk Pandelidis, MD, who noted that he and a number of other psychiatrists had tried to form a Hellenic Psychiatric Society in 1966. The attempt did not work out. Dr. Pandelidis was asked to write a short article about that effort for the HAPA Newsletter.

Dr. Alexopoulos, HAPA Secretary, was unable to attend the meeting due to weather conditions. Dr. Lymberis functioned as the Secretary for this meeting.

III. MEMBERSHIP

Dr. Lymberis thanked Dr. Cardasis for his work as Chair of the HAPA Membership Committee. He has organized the HAPA Directory and is working on membership recruitment. He clearly needs everyone's help. Our goal is to reach 100 HAPA members so we can be formally recognized in the APA Assembly as an Affiliate organization. In 1999, HAPA had 37 dues-paying members. Of these, three were MITs and five were Affiliate Members. We clearly have a long way to go.

IV. AMENDMENTS

Amendments to the HAPA By-Laws were passed without any changes as distributed and are effective as of the conclusion of this meeting.

1. ARTICLE III, Membership — Delete Section 2b, Corresponding Members. This section is not needed. General and corresponding members have the same dues. HAPA has no requirement for attendance at HAPA Annual Meetings.

2. ARTICLE IV, Officers and Executive Council — Section 3, Elections and Term of Office: “The following officers shall be elected at the Annual Meetings of HAPA for a three (3) year term: President, President-Elect, Secretary and Treasurer. The President shall serve as a member of the Executive Committee for three (3) additional years upon completion of his or her term of office as President and shall not be eligible for reelection as President-Elect until four (4) years after completing a term as President.”

3. ARTICLE V, Committees — “Committee Chairpersons of all committees are appointed by the President for three (3) years and their term of office expires with the expiration of the term of office of the President who appointed them.”

4. ARTICLE V, Committees — Add to Section 4, Committee Membership: “All HAPA Committees shall have a minimum of three (3) members.”

5. ARTICLE VII, Finance — Amend “HAPA's books shall be audited annually” to “The President and/or the Executive Committee can request an audit of HAPA books when or if it is needed.”

6. ADDITION — ARTICLE XII, Dissolution: “In the unlikely event of the dissolution of HAPA, the President shall appoint a Liquidation Committee. Such committee will proceed to liquidate all of the physical assets and legal contracts of any and all forms of HAPA in accordance with state and federal laws and procedures.”

V. ELECTIONS

Dr. Charalambous was elected for the term of office through 2003.

VI. ANNUAL HAPA MEETING

The Annual HAPA Meeting time is to change to a later day and time. Specifically, the change will be to the Tuesday of the APA Meeting and to a dinner meeting. This change is believed to help with attendance by members from abroad.

VII. HAPA MEETING IN GREECE

Explore the feasibility of a HAPA meeting in Greece for 2002. George Christodoulou noted that Drs. Zervas, Vaslamatzis and Lyketsos could work on this. The suggestion was made by Dr. Lymberis to also include Peter Partocolis in the feasibility phase of the discussions.

VIII. HAPA TASKS FOR 2000–2001

1. HAPA Membership Drive: contact the APA Membership Office and get labels for the East Coast, Illinois, Ohio and California where there are many Hellenic members, and send them all a letter with an application for membership. Post a HAPA Membership Drive notice to all district branch newsletters. This will be done by the HAPA President.

2. Explore the possibility of establishing a HAPA Scholarship Fund from donations by large Greek foundations, such as the Onassis and Latsis Foundations. HAPA could thus offer a scholarship to Greek psychiatrists for post-graduate training in psychiatry in the United States. The HAPA President will write to both foundations.

3. HAPA needs all members to try to get funds from pharmaceutical companies for our next annual meeting and our newsletter. HAPA is our organization — we all need to help. Start now! Dr. Lymberis will contact Zeneca since they have helped us from the beginning.

4. The presenters in our scientific meetings will be asked to submit summaries of their presentations for the HAPA Newsletter at the time of their presentations.

5. Initiate a HAPA project to work with the Greek Orthodox Church. Dr. Kalogerakis mentioned the exchange of correspondence he has had with His Eminence Archbishop Demetrios. He recommended that “what is needed is a formal approach to the Archdiocese in the United States by HAPA, which is the only organization representing Greek-American psychiatrists in this country.” We need to initiate a dialogue on common interests. The HAPA President appointed Dr. Kalogerakis to Chair the HAPA Greek Clergy Project and report at the next meeting.

IX. SCIENTIFIC PROGRAMME

Due to time limitations, Dr. Lymberis' presentation was postponed to a future meeting. The two other scheduled presentations were received with great interest and generated a lively discussion.

The meeting was adjourned at 3:00 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,
Maria T. Lymberis, M.D.

15 Μαΐου 2000 — Σικάγο, Ιλινόι

Η συνάντηση κηρύχθηκε σε έναρξη στις 12:30 μ.μ. από την Maria T. Lymberis, MD, Πρόεδρο της HAPA, η οποία καλωσόρισε μέλη και προσκεκλημένους.

Ι. Τα πρακτικά της Ιδρυτικής Συνάντησης του Οκτωβρίου 1999 εγκρίθηκαν όπως δημοσιεύθηκαν στο ενημερωτικό δελτίο και στην ιστοσελίδα, με τη διόρθωση ότι η Linda Kalivas ήταν παρούσα.

ΙΙ. ΕΚΘΕΣΗ ΠΡΟΕΔΡΟΥ

Η Dr Lymberis εξέφρασε την εκτίμησή της για τη στήριξη της AstraZeneca στις επιστημονικές μας συναντήσεις για δεύτερη χρονιά. Παραμένουμε μια πολύ νέα εταιρεία με περιορισμένους πόρους και μεγάλα σχέδια. Η χρονιά αφιερώθηκε στην ανάπτυξη των βασικών δομών με ελάχιστη εξωτερική χρηματοδότηση και μικρή βάση συνδρομών. Ευχαρίστησε τον γιο της Anthony De Cordoba, ο οποίος πρόσφερε αφιλοκερδώς τον χρόνο και την τεχνογνωσία του σχεδιάζοντας το λογότυπο και την ιστοσελίδα, που τέθηκε σε λειτουργία τον Απρίλιο του 2000. Ευχαρίστησε επίσης τον σύζυγό της, Pedro De Cordoba, για την πολύτιμη βοήθειά του στα ζητήματα μελών, τραπεζικών συναλλαγών και αλληλογραφίας.

Η Dr Lymberis ανακοίνωσε σημαντικές συναντήσεις που θα γίνονταν στην Ελλάδα εκείνη τη χρονιά: το 5ο Διεθνές Ψυχαναλυτικό Συμπόσιο των Δελφών «Αυτογνωσία: πριν και μετά τον Φρόιντ», 25–30 Ιουλίου 2000· το 2ο Διεθνές Συνέδριο «Ορμόνες, Εγκέφαλος και Νευροψυχοφαρμακολογία» στη Ρόδο, 15–19 Ιουλίου 2000· και το 11ο Συνέδριο της Ελληνικής Εταιρείας Ψυχαναλυτικής Ψυχοθεραπείας στην Αθήνα, 23–26 Νοεμβρίου 2000.

Ο Γραμματέας Dr Alexopoulos δεν μπόρεσε να παρευρεθεί λόγω καιρικών συνθηκών· χρέη γραμματέα εκτέλεσε η Dr Lymberis.

ΙΙΙ. ΜΕΛΗ

Η Dr Lymberis ευχαρίστησε τον Dr Cardasis για το έργο του ως Προέδρου της Επιτροπής Μελών. Έχει οργανώσει τον κατάλογο μελών και εργάζεται για την προσέλκυση νέων. Στόχος μας είναι τα 100 μέλη, ώστε να αναγνωριστούμε επίσημα από τη Συνέλευση της APA ως συνδεδεμένος φορέας. Το 1999 η HAPA είχε 37 μέλη με καταβεβλημένη συνδρομή.

IV. ΤΡΟΠΟΠΟΙΗΣΕΙΣ ΚΑΤΑΣΤΑΤΙΚΟΥ

Οι τροποποιήσεις εγκρίθηκαν χωρίς αλλαγές και ισχύουν από τη λήξη της συνάντησης: κατάργηση της κατηγορίας των ανταποκριτών μελών· τριετής θητεία για Πρόεδρο, Εκλεγμένο Πρόεδρο, Γραμματέα και Ταμία· τριετής θητεία για τους προέδρους επιτροπών· ελάχιστος αριθμός τριών μελών ανά επιτροπή· έλεγχος βιβλίων κατόπιν αιτήματος του Προέδρου ή της Εκτελεστικής Επιτροπής· και προσθήκη άρθρου για τη διάλυση της εταιρείας.

V. ΕΚΛΟΓΕΣ

Ο Dr Charalambous εκλέχθηκε για θητεία έως το 2003.

VI. ΕΤΗΣΙΑ ΣΥΝΑΝΤΗΣΗ

Η ώρα της ετήσιας συνάντησης αλλάζει: θα γίνεται την Τρίτη της Συνάντησης της APA, ως δείπνο. Η αλλαγή αναμένεται να διευκολύνει τη συμμετοχή μελών από το εξωτερικό.

VII. ΣΥΝΑΝΤΗΣΗ ΣΤΗΝ ΕΛΛΑΔΑ

Να διερευνηθεί η δυνατότητα συνάντησης της HAPA στην Ελλάδα το 2002.

VIII. ΣΤΟΧΟΙ 2000–2001

1. Εκστρατεία προσέλκυσης μελών μέσω της APA. 2. Διερεύνηση ίδρυσης ταμείου υποτροφιών με δωρεές από μεγάλα ελληνικά ιδρύματα, ώστε η HAPA να προσφέρει υποτροφία σε Έλληνες ψυχιάτρους για μεταπτυχιακή εκπαίδευση στις ΗΠΑ. 3. Αναζήτηση χρηματοδότησης για την επόμενη ετήσια συνάντηση και το ενημερωτικό δελτίο. 4. Οι ομιλητές θα καταθέτουν περίληψη της παρουσίασής τους. 5. Έναρξη προγράμματος συνεργασίας με την Ελληνική Ορθόδοξη Εκκλησία· ο Dr Kalogerakis ορίστηκε πρόεδρος του σχετικού έργου.

IX. ΕΠΙΣΤΗΜΟΝΙΚΟ ΠΡΟΓΡΑΜΜΑ

Λόγω περιορισμένου χρόνου η παρουσίαση της Dr Lymberis αναβλήθηκε. Οι δύο άλλες προγραμματισμένες παρουσιάσεις έγιναν δεκτές με μεγάλο ενδιαφέρον.

Η συνάντηση έληξε στις 3:00 μ.μ.

Με εκτίμηση,
Maria T. Lymberis, M.D.

body.en:
The Steering Committee for the establishment of HAPA organized this meeting.

Chair: Maria T. Lymberis, MD
Members: George Alexopoulos, MD · Anthony Kales, MD · Michael Kalogerakis, MD · Constantine Lyketsos, MD · Miltiades Zaphiropoulos, MD

I: CALL TO ORDER AND INTRODUCTORY REMARKS

The inaugural meeting of the Hellenic American Psychiatric Association (HAPA) was called to order at 12:15 by the Chair of the Steering Committee Maria T. Lymberis, M.D. Dr. Lymberis thanked the attendees for their presence and support in making the founding of HAPA a reality. She noted that it was her election as APA Treasurer that made it possible for her to generate momentum for the establishment of HAPA. Throughout her 30 years of active service in APA, she was acutely aware of the lack of any Hellenic psychiatric organization. She noted that APA has many leaders and active contributors of Greek origin, as well as many others who are hellenically identified. She specifically cited Dr. Miltiades Zaphiropoulos, the APA Assembly Speaker at the time she first started her APA service, as a major source of inspiration. She then thanked the members of the Steering Committee for their help in making HAPA a reality.

Dr. Lymberis then introduced his Excellency, Alexander Philon, the Greek Ambassador to the United States, who presented welcoming remarks that were highly supportive of HAPA. Mr. Philon was followed on the podium by George N. Christodoulou, M.D., Professor and Chairman of the Department of Psychiatry at the University of Athens and the President of the Hellenic Psychiatric Association. Dr. Christodoulou presented warm wishes and support from the Hellenic Psychiatric Association to the inaugural meeting of HAPA. He stressed the strong commitment on his part, of his association and of psychiatrists in Greece to work closely with HAPA in accomplishing its mission and establish close collaboration.

II: BUSINESS MEETING

The first business meeting of HAPA was presided over by Dr. Lymberis. The following issues were presented:

(1) The HAPA By-Laws

Dr. Lymberis explained that she drafted the HAPA By-Laws from those of the Academy of Psychiatry & Law, the Indo-American Psychiatric Association and the NY Hellenic Medical Society with the assistance of Dr. Zaphiropoulos. Dr. Christodoulou moved that psychiatrist members of the Hellenic Psychiatric Association should be full members of HAPA. This motion was discussed. Dr. Lymberis explained that the By-Laws were drafted so that HAPA will not spend its limited resources in processing membership applications (i.e. verifying credentials). As presently drafted, the HAPA Membership Committee will only need to verify that the applicants are members in good standing in APA and AACAP, thus relying on those organizations for verification of credentials. In view of this clarification, Dr. Lyketsos proposed the following action: it was moved, seconded and passed that psychiatrist members of the HPA will be full HAPA members provided they submit a letter from the HPA documenting they are members in good standing.

The mission statement of HAPA was then discussed. Dr. Lymberis explained that she drafted Article II of the By-Laws (Mission Statement) with the aim of being inclusive. Specifically, to include not just psychiatrists of Greek origin, but those who are connected to the Hellenic heritage and the spirit of Hellenism. In addition, to include the full spectrum of professionals involved in research, teaching or practice within the bio-psycho-social model of modern psychiatry. There was unanimous support for this position and Article II was passed.

The offices and committees were also discussed, suggestions were made and were passed in principle.

ACTION: It was moved, seconded and passed that
a) The submitted HAPA By-Laws be accepted in principle with changes in membership categories as amended.
b) The By-Laws Committee, chaired by Dr. Lymberis with Drs. Lyketsos, Zaphiropoulos and Zervas, will further amend the By-Laws and submit the amended By-Laws for approval at the First Annual HAPA meeting in Chicago, May 2000.

(2) HAPA ELECTIONS

Dr. Lymberis asked Dr. Lyketsos to present the slate of officers put forth by the HAPA Steering Committee. She also invited nominations from the floor for Councilors. Additional nominations for HAPA officers were also sought from the floor but none were forthcoming. Elections were held and the following officers and councilors were unanimously elected:

President (1999–2001): Maria T. Lymberis, M.D.
President Elect (1999–2001): Constantine G. Lyketsos, M.D.
Secretary (1999–2001): George Alexopoulos, M.D.
Treasurer (1999–2001): Dora Wang, M.D.
Councilor (1999–2002): George N. Christodoulou, M.D.
Councilor (1999–2001): William C. Cardasis, M.D.
Councilor (1999–2000): Kanellos Charalambous, M.D.

(3) HAPA COMMITTEES

Dr. Lymberis requested further discussion of HAPA's constitutional committees. Specifically, the need for members for key HAPA Committees such as:

a) The Program Committee, to develop the scientific presentation for the First Annual HAPA meeting for May 2000 in Chicago. Dr. Lyketsos agreed to be Chair with Dr. Kalogerakis as Co-Chair and George Petrides, M.D. as member. CME credit was not possible for the present meeting but efforts will be made to get CME for subsequent meetings. The discussion that followed included efforts to showcase the work of Greek-American psychiatrists and to highlight issues regarding the psychiatric needs or problems of Greek-Americans in the US, in Greece or in other countries.

b) The Membership Committee: William Cardasis, M.D. agreed to Chair this committee with Dr. Ioannis Zervas as Co-Chair in charge of the HPA applications for HAPA membership. This committee will develop a HAPA database, a directory and strategies for membership recruitment. The Hellenic Medical Societies of New York and Chicago as well as the APA and HPA could be contacted in a recruitment effort.

c) The Newsletter Committee: Stephanie Spanos, M.D. agreed to Chair this committee with Dr. Helen Papastrat as Co-Chair. This committee will publish at least one issue of the HAPA Newsletter per year.

III: SCIENTIFIC PRESENTATION

The business meeting was followed by an excellent scientific presentation on “Depression in Old Age and Vascular Depression” by Dr. George Alexopoulos, Professor of Psychiatry and Director of the Institute of Geriatric Psychiatry at Cornell University, Westchester Division in New York. Dr. Alexopoulos' presentation discussed the epidemiology of depression and old age, and presented the evidence for the hypothesis that his group developed that one of the causes of this depression is cerebrovascular disease affecting the subcortical white matter of the brain. The presentation drew a lot of praise. The discussion was lively. Clearly HAPA's first scientific presentation showcased excellence in research by a Greek psychiatrist. More to follow!

IV: ADJOURNMENT

The first annual HAPA meeting was adjourned at 2:30 pm. The next annual HAPA meeting has preliminarily been set for Monday, May 15, 2000, 9:00 AM to 1:00 PM in Chicago, IL in conjunction with the American Psychiatric Association Annual Meeting.

FOUNDING MEMBERS OF HAPA

The founding of HAPA was attended by the following:

George Alexopoulos · William Cardasis · Lakis Charalampous · George Christodoulou · Nicholas Dunkas · Edward Hanin · Charles Huffine · Michael Kalogerakis · Roubinis Kambolis · Petros Levounis · Maria T. Lymberis · Helen Papastrat · Georgios Petrides · Stephanie Spanos · Miltiades Zaphiropoulos · Ioannis Zervas · Theodoros Ziongas

Unable to attend: Emmanuil Cassimatis · James Chengelis · Rossetos Gournellis · Linda Kalivas · Ioannis Liappas · Angeline Stergiou · Nicholas Stratas · Nikos Vaidakis · Heiman Van Dam

Respectfully submitted,
Maria T. Lymberis, M.D.
Constantine Lyketsos, M.D.
body.el:
Η Συντονιστική Επιτροπή για την ίδρυση της HAPA διοργάνωσε αυτή τη συνάντηση.

Πρόεδρος: Maria T. Lymberis, MD
Μέλη: George Alexopoulos, MD · Anthony Kales, MD · Michael Kalogerakis, MD · Constantine Lyketsos, MD · Miltiades Zaphiropoulos, MD

Ι: ΕΝΑΡΞΗ ΚΑΙ ΕΙΣΑΓΩΓΙΚΕΣ ΠΑΡΑΤΗΡΗΣΕΙΣ

Η ιδρυτική συνάντηση της Ελληνοαμερικανικής Ψυχιατρικής Εταιρείας (HAPA) κηρύχθηκε σε έναρξη στις 12:15 από την Πρόεδρο της Συντονιστικής Επιτροπής, Maria T. Lymberis, M.D. Η Dr Lymberis ευχαρίστησε τους παρευρισκόμενους για την παρουσία και τη στήριξή τους στην πραγματοποίηση της ίδρυσης της HAPA. Σημείωσε ότι η εκλογή της ως Ταμία της APA ήταν εκείνη που της επέτρεψε να δώσει ώθηση στην ίδρυση της εταιρείας. Στα τριάντα χρόνια ενεργού υπηρεσίας της στην APA είχε συνειδητοποιήσει έντονα την απουσία οποιουδήποτε ελληνικού ψυχιατρικού φορέα. Επισήμανε ότι η APA έχει πολλούς ηγέτες και ενεργούς συνεισφέροντες ελληνικής καταγωγής, καθώς και πολλούς άλλους που ταυτίζονται με τον ελληνισμό. Αναφέρθηκε ειδικά στον Dr Miltiades Zaphiropoulos ως σημαντική πηγή έμπνευσης. Στη συνέχεια ευχαρίστησε τα μέλη της Συντονιστικής Επιτροπής.

Η Dr Lymberis παρουσίασε τον Εξοχότατο Αλέξανδρο Φίλωνα, Πρέσβη της Ελλάδας στις Ηνωμένες Πολιτείες, ο οποίος απηύθυνε χαιρετισμό με έντονη στήριξη προς τη HAPA. Ακολούθησε ο George N. Christodoulou, M.D., Καθηγητής και Διευθυντής της Ψυχιατρικής Κλινικής του Πανεπιστημίου Αθηνών και Πρόεδρος της Ελληνικής Ψυχιατρικής Εταιρείας, ο οποίος μετέφερε θερμές ευχές και στήριξη. Τόνισε τη δέσμευση, τη δική του και της εταιρείας του, για στενή συνεργασία με τη HAPA.

ΙΙ: ΔΙΟΙΚΗΤΙΚΗ ΣΥΝΕΔΡΙΑΣΗ

Της πρώτης διοικητικής συνεδρίασης προήδρευσε η Dr Lymberis. Συζητήθηκαν τα εξής:

(1) Το Καταστατικό της HAPA

Η Dr Lymberis εξήγησε ότι συνέταξε το καταστατικό με βάση εκείνα της Academy of Psychiatry & Law, της Indo-American Psychiatric Association και της Hellenic Medical Society της Νέας Υόρκης, με τη βοήθεια του Dr Zaphiropoulos. Ο Dr Christodoulou πρότεινε τα μέλη-ψυχίατροι της Ελληνικής Ψυχιατρικής Εταιρείας να είναι πλήρη μέλη της HAPA. Μετά από συζήτηση, και δεδομένου ότι το καταστατικό συντάχθηκε ώστε η HAPA να μη δαπανά τους περιορισμένους πόρους της στον έλεγχο των τίτλων, αποφασίστηκε ομόφωνα ότι τα μέλη-ψυχίατροι της Ελληνικής Ψυχιατρικής Εταιρείας θα είναι πλήρη μέλη εφόσον προσκομίζουν βεβαίωση ότι είναι ενεργά μέλη της.

Συζητήθηκε στη συνέχεια η διακήρυξη αποστολής. Η Dr Lymberis εξήγησε ότι συνέταξε το Άρθρο ΙΙ με στόχο τη μεγαλύτερη δυνατή συμπερίληψη: όχι μόνο ψυχιάτρους ελληνικής καταγωγής, αλλά και όσους συνδέονται με την ελληνική κληρονομιά και το πνεύμα του ελληνισμού, καθώς και το σύνολο των επαγγελματιών που ασχολούνται με την έρευνα, τη διδασκαλία ή την άσκηση της σύγχρονης ψυχιατρικής στο βιοψυχοκοινωνικό μοντέλο. Το Άρθρο ΙΙ εγκρίθηκε ομόφωνα.

Συζητήθηκαν επίσης τα αξιώματα και οι επιτροπές και εγκρίθηκαν κατ' αρχήν.

ΑΠΟΦΑΣΗ: Εγκρίθηκε ότι
α) Το υποβληθέν καταστατικό γίνεται δεκτό κατ' αρχήν, με τις τροποποιήσεις στις κατηγορίες μελών.
β) Η Επιτροπή Καταστατικού, με πρόεδρο την Dr Lymberis και μέλη τους Dr Lyketsos, Zaphiropoulos και Zervas, θα το επεξεργαστεί περαιτέρω και θα το υποβάλει προς έγκριση στην Πρώτη Ετήσια Συνάντηση στο Σικάγο, τον Μάιο του 2000.

(2) ΕΚΛΟΓΕΣ

Εκλέχθηκαν ομόφωνα:

Εκλεγμένος Πρόεδρος (1999–2001): Constantine G. Lyketsos, M.D.

Σύμβουλος (1999–2000): Kanellos Charalambous, M.D.

(3) ΕΠΙΤΡΟΠΕΣ

α) Επιτροπή Προγράμματος, για την επιστημονική εκδήλωση της Πρώτης Ετήσιας Συνάντησης του Μαΐου 2000 στο Σικάγο. Πρόεδρος ο Dr Lyketsos, αντιπρόεδρος ο Dr Kalogerakis και μέλος ο George Petrides, M.D. Μονάδες συνεχιζόμενης εκπαίδευσης δεν ήταν εφικτές για την τρέχουσα συνάντηση, θα γίνουν όμως προσπάθειες για τις επόμενες.

β) Επιτροπή Μελών: πρόεδρος ο William Cardasis, M.D., αντιπρόεδρος ο Dr Ιωάννης Ζέρβας, υπεύθυνος για τις αιτήσεις από την Ελληνική Ψυχιατρική Εταιρεία. Η επιτροπή θα αναπτύξει βάση δεδομένων, κατάλογο μελών και στρατηγικές προσέλκυσης.

γ) Επιτροπή Ενημερωτικού Δελτίου: πρόεδρος η Stephanie Spanos, M.D., αντιπρόεδρος η Dr Helen Papastrat. Η επιτροπή θα εκδίδει τουλάχιστον ένα τεύχος τον χρόνο.

ΙΙΙ: ΕΠΙΣΤΗΜΟΝΙΚΗ ΠΑΡΟΥΣΙΑΣΗ

Ακολούθησε εξαιρετική επιστημονική παρουσίαση με θέμα «Κατάθλιψη στην τρίτη ηλικία και αγγειακή κατάθλιψη» από τον Dr George Alexopoulos, Καθηγητή Ψυχιατρικής και Διευθυντή του Institute of Geriatric Psychiatry του Πανεπιστημίου Cornell. Η παρουσίαση αφορούσε την επιδημιολογία της κατάθλιψης στην τρίτη ηλικία και τα ευρήματα που στηρίζουν την υπόθεση ότι μία από τις αιτίες της είναι η αγγειακή νόσος που προσβάλλει τη λευκή ουσία του εγκεφάλου. Η συζήτηση που ακολούθησε ήταν ζωηρή.

body.en:
HELLENIC AMERICAN PSYCHIATRIC ASSOCIATION — Announcement to Greek psychiatrists

Dear colleagues,

Following the efforts of the HAPA board, an important financial agreement has been reached with the administration of the American Psychiatric Association (APA) for Greek psychiatrists who live and practise in Greece and who register for the first time as international members of the APA.

The agreement provides a 35% discount on the first year of membership (that is, 10% on top of the existing individual discount) and up to 25% off the annual international membership subscription in the years that follow. It applies to Greek psychiatrists joining for the first time as new international members.

In detail:
• 35% discount for the first year (10% on top of the standing 25%) for every Greek psychiatrist registering as a new international member, whether individually or as part of a group.
• Up to 50 new APA international members: 10% off the annual subscription.
• 50–150 new APA international members: 20% off the annual subscription.
• More than 150 new international members: 25% off the annual subscription.

The annual APA subscription for members from Greece (before the discounts above) is: International members/fellows/distinguished fellows $214.00 USD per year; international residents $39.00 USD per year; international medical students free.

HAPA is an official affiliated member of the APA and can coordinate and complete the group registration of its members as new APA members.

Benefits for APA international members (including fellows and distinguished fellows) include free or discounted access to 200+ online psychiatry courses and activities, the free Members' Course of the Month, a free online subscription to the American Journal of Psychiatry and a subscription to Psychiatric News (value $301.00 USD), a discounted online subscription to Psychiatric Services (value $22.00 USD), registration discounts for the Annual Meeting (value $625.00 USD) and for IPS: The Mental Health Services Conference (value $195.00 USD), and 20% off more than 700 books and special pricing on journals through APA Publishing.

Benefits for international resident members include free access to the supplementary education and training programme with online courses; free online subscriptions to the American Journal of Psychiatry (value $301.00 USD) and the Resident's Journal, Psychiatric Services (value $146.00 USD), Focus: The Journal for Lifelong Learning in Psychiatry (value $249.00 USD), Psychiatric News and the Resident's Forum; registration discounts for the Annual Meeting (value $70.00 USD) and IPS (value $65.00–95.00 USD); and 25% off more than 700 books and special pricing on journals through APA Publishing, including US board examination preparation material.

With respect,
Georgios Karampoutakis, MD, MSc, PhD — President-Elect
