Αγαπητοί Συνάδελφοι,

Σας ενημερώνουμε ότι μετά από ενέργειες του Δ.Σ. της Hellenic American Psychiatric Association (HAPA) επετεύχθη σημαντική οικονομική συμφωνία με την διοίκηση της American Psychiatric Association (APA), η οποία αφορά τους Έλληνες Ψυχιάτρους που κατοικούν και δραστηριοποιούνται επαγγελματικά στην Ελλάδα και οι οποίοι θα εγγραφούν για πρώτη φορά ως διεθνή μέλη στην American Psychiatric Association.

Η οικονομική συμφωνία περιλαμβάνει σημαντικές εκπτώσεις στο κόστος εγγραφής ύψους 35% για το 1ο έτος εγγραφής (δηλαδή 10% επιπλέον της υπάρχουσας έκπτωσης ατομικής εγγραφής) και έως 25% έκπτωση στην ετήσια συνδρομή διεθνούς μέλους για τα επόμενα έτη. Η αναφερόμενη συμφωνία αφορά ομαδική εγγραφή Ελλήνων Ψυχιάτρων που θα εγγραφούν για πρώτη φορά ως νέα διεθνή μέλη στην APA.

Αναλυτικότερα η συμφωνία προβλέπει:
• 35% έκπτωση για τον 1ο χρόνο (10% επιπλέον του ισχύοντος 25%), για κάθε Έλληνα Ψυχίατρο που θα εγγραφεί ως νέο διεθνές μέλος ανεξαρτήτως αν γίνει ατομική ή ομαδική εγγραφή.
• Εγγραφή έως 50 νέων διεθνών μελών APA: 10% έκπτωση στην ετήσια συνδρομή μέλους.
• Εγγραφή 50–150 νέων διεθνών μελών APA: 20% έκπτωση στην ετήσια συνδρομή μέλους.
• Εγγραφή περισσότερων των 150 νέων διεθνών μελών: 25% έκπτωση στην ετήσια συνδρομή μέλους.

Το ποσό της ετήσιας συνδρομής μπορεί να μειωθεί περαιτέρω, εάν ο αριθμός των Ελλήνων Ψυχιάτρων κατά την αρχική ομαδική εγγραφή είναι πολύ μεγαλύτερος.

Το ετήσιο ποσό συνδρομής στην APA για μέλη από την Ελλάδα (χωρίς υπολογισμό των ανωτέρω εκπτώσεων) έχει ως εξής: Διεθνή Μέλη/Συνεργάτες/Διακεκριμένοι Συνεργάτες $214.00 USD ετησίως· Διεθνείς Ειδικευόμενοι $39.00 USD ετησίως· Διεθνείς Φοιτητές Ιατρικής δωρεάν.

summary.el: Η διάκριση απονεμήθηκε στις 20 Μαΐου 2013 για τη συμβολή του στη γηριατρική ψυχιατρική.

body.en:
During the APA 57th Convocation of Distinguished Fellows, May 20th 2013, San Francisco, CA

This Special Presidential Commendation is awarded in recognition of Dr Alexopoulos' seminal contributions to research, training and clinical care in geriatric psychiatry.

Dr Alexopoulos is the S.P. Tobin and A.M. Cooper Professor, Professor of the Graduate School of Medical Sciences and Vice Chairman for Geriatric Psychiatry at Weill Medical College of Cornell University. He founded the Weill-Cornell Institute of Geriatric Psychiatry and still serves as its director. He is also the director of the NIMH-supported Advanced Center for Interventions and Services Research in Geriatric Mood Disorders.

Dr Alexopoulos received his medical degree from the National University of Athens, Greece. He was initially trained at New Jersey Medical School and completed his psychiatric residency at Cornell University Medical College, where he also held his research fellowship in psychobiology. He has received four consecutive centre grants from the NIMH as well as individual (R01) grants, and has been the director of the T32 NIMH Research Fellowship in Geriatric Mood Disorders since 1989.

Dr Alexopoulos is the editor for the Western Hemisphere of the International Journal of Geriatric Psychiatry and sits on the editorial boards of other professional journals. He has received numerous awards, including the research award of the International College of Geriatric Psychoneuropharmacology, the APA Greenberg Award and the American College of Psychiatrists' Geriatric Research Award.

body.en:
February 2013 — Greetings from HAPA

The HAPA executive committee invites you to join us on May 21st 2013 for the 14th annual meeting of HAPA at the San Francisco Marriott Marquis. This year HAPA features two very special presentations. One from Greece: “The Women's Mental Health Clinic at Eginition Hospital, Athens, Greece: the first ten years” by Iannis Zervas, MD, Associate Professor of Psychiatry, Athens University Medical School and Chief of the Women's Mental Health & Perinatal Psychiatry Clinic at Eginition Hospital. The other from the US: “Improving the quality of medical education worldwide: the contributions of ECFMG and FAIMER” by Emmanuel Cassimatis, MD, DFAPA, Professor of Psychiatry, F. Edward Hébert School of Medicine, USUHS; President and CEO, Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates; Chair of the Board of Directors, Foundation for Advancement of International Medical Education and Research. Both are timely and relevant, addressing current central concerns.

The Hellenic American Psychiatric Association is the only Hellenic psychiatric group in the APA promoting communication and addressing vital issues of interest to Greek or Hellenophile psychiatrists living in the US, Greece and the Greek diaspora. The association meets annually on the Tuesday evening of the APA annual meeting at 6:00 PM. The executive committee meets monthly by teleconference. All HAPA business is done on a volunteer basis, mainly online. HAPA is in the process of establishing a foundation to fulfil its mission and advance its scientific and professional goals, including funding a postgraduate fellowship for aspiring psychiatrists to further their professional development in any clinical or research area of interest.

The business meeting follows the scientific presentation. A Dutch-treat dinner at a gourmet restaurant with local flavours wraps up the evening in a relaxed, enjoyable atmosphere. The annual meetings are exciting opportunities to see good friends, network, discover new friends and share cultural and professional experiences. Greek American psychiatrists need a home in the APA, and HAPA fulfils that need.

Membership dues are $52.00 for general members and $27.00 for members-in-training.

See you in San Francisco.

title.en: Recent publications by HAPA members
title.el: Πρόσφατες δημοσιεύσεις μελών της HAPA

summary.en: Books by Philip Candilis and Petros Levounis, and an article by Nick Bouras on the modern Hellenic medical diaspora.
summary.el: Βιβλία των Philip Candilis και Πέτρου Λεβούνη και άρθρο του Νίκου Μπούρα για τη σύγχρονη ελληνική ιατρική διασπορά.

body.en:
Several HAPA members have recently published very worthwhile books or articles. The following are worthy of your attention.

1) Forensic Ethics and the Expert Witness — Philip J. Candilis (University of Massachusetts Medical School), Robert Weinstock (UCLA) and Richard Martinez (University of Colorado Health Sciences Center / Denver Health Medical Center). Springer Publishing, New York, 2010.

From the cover: the expert witness's job is often described as a balancing act — duty to clients on the one hand, duty to society on the other. Forensic Ethics and the Expert Witness probes beyond the familiar conflict-of-interest and overlapping-roles framework to present a new model of professional ethics. Richly illustrated with cases from medicine, psychiatry and law, this elegantly written volume examines the common moral ground linking these usually separate domains, and relates forensic ethics to larger concepts of morality and justice. In this integrative approach the expert witness is redefined as one who can balance professional with societal and personal codes, in what the authors call “robust professionalism”.

2) Handbook of Motivation and Change: A Practical Guide for Clinicians — Petros Levounis, M.D., M.A. and Bachaar Arnaout, M.D. APPI Press, 2010.

A busy clinician's guide to motivational interviewing. With a special focus on substance use disorders and addiction, the handbook equips readers with a full understanding of the motivational interviewing approach — an understanding that can be applied flexibly to patients' issues of motivation and change well beyond substance use. It is written by more than twenty practitioners of different psychotherapies who employ motivational work, and features case studies punctuated by film references, practical suggestions for treatment and trainee supervision, and summary key points and multiple-choice questions. The authors focus on interventions ranging from psychopharmacology to support groups, address the challenges of treating patients at various stages of life, examine how motivational work can change the culture of an organisation, and discuss the evidence base of this effective and compelling therapy.

3) “A historical account of modern Hellenic medical diaspora” — N. Bouras, Institute of Psychiatry, King's College London. Archives of Hellenic Medicine 2009, 26(2):151–159.

There has been increasing interest in recent years in the Greek diaspora. Very little is known, however, about the role of Greek physicians and biomedical scientists of the diaspora and their contributions. The physician of King Charles II was Greek, and other well-known doctors of the diaspora included Adamantios Korais, pioneer of the Greek Enlightenment; Iakovos Pylarinos, an early contributor to immunisation against smallpox; Constantin von Economo, who described encephalitis lethargica; and George Papanikolaou, the originator of the Pap test. The World Hellenic BioMedical Association was the first structured initiative to bring together the Hellenic biomedical diaspora in contemporary times. The First World Congress of the Hellenic Medical Diaspora was organised in Athens in 1990 in collaboration with the Athens Medical Society; since then eight more world congresses have been organised in Athens, Cyprus and New York. This article presents the activities of the World Hellenic BioMedical Association from 1990 to 2008 and comments on the strengths and weaknesses of the overall endeavour.

We welcome other submissions.

summary.el: Μνήμη του Michael G. Kalogerakis, πρώην προέδρου της ASAP και κλινικού καθηγητή στο NYU.

body.en:
We note with sadness the passing of our colleague and dear friend, Dr Michael G. Kalogerakis, past president of the American Society for Adolescent Psychiatry and of the International Society for Psychiatry and Psychology. He was also Clinical Professor of Psychiatry at NYU School of Medicine, the former Director of Adolescent Services at Bellevue Psychiatric Hospital, and the former Associate Commissioner for Children and Youth, New York State Office of Mental Health. He served for 25 years as a board member of the Citizens' Committee for Children of New York, the oldest child advocacy organisation in the US, and was President of the Kenworthy-Swift Foundation. Michael had an influence on many through his work in the community, teaching, writing and clinical work. Our organisations benefited immeasurably from his wise leadership. The field of adolescent psychiatry is richer because of his many contributions to the scientific literature, as well as his teaching. We extend sincere condolences to his bereaved family.

Dr Joseph Kenan, President, ASAP, and Dr Patricia Garel, President, ISAPP

March 19, 2010

Dr Michael Kalogerakis was my first teacher in adolescent psychiatry. He was the unit chief of Ward PQ-5, the adolescent psychiatry ward at Bellevue Hospital, when I was a medical student doing an elective in adolescent psychiatry. He was a Clinical Professor of Psychiatry at NYU School of Medicine. He edited one of the major sections (Treatment) in ASAP's Textbook of Adolescent Psychiatry. He was chair of the Committee on Adolescent Sexuality of the New York chapter of ASAP during the years I was a member of that committee. He went on to become Associate Commissioner for Children and Youth in the New York State Office of Mental Hygiene. He organised the first weekend conference on juvenile delinquency at NYU Medical Center. Of course, he was a past president of ASAP and a past president of the International Society for Adolescent Psychiatry, and I believe also a past president of the Pan-American Society for Adolescent Psychiatry. He will be missed.

Richard Rosner, M.D., F.A.S.A.P., D.L.F.A.P.A., F.A.C.Psych.

3) Minutes of the HAPA Executive Committee, 15 October 2007

On Monday, October 15, 2007, George Petrides, MD opened the HAPA Executive Committee teleconference at 5:00 PM EST. Participants: Dr George Petrides, President; Dr Maria Lymberis, HAPA Founder and Past President; Dr Manolis Cassimatis, President-Elect. Dr Petrides reported on his recent trip to Greece where he represented HAPA at the meeting of the Eastern European Psychiatric Association (EEPA). This very successful conference was held in Thessaloniki under the auspices of the World Psychiatric Association. It was organised by our distinguished colleague, HAPA member and past HAPA officer Dr George Christodoulou, President of the EEPA and immediate past President of the Hellenic Psychiatric Association.

While in Greece Dr Petrides had the opportunity to speak with several Greek colleagues, including Dr George Papadimitriou, recently elected Professor and Chair of the Department of Psychiatry at the University of Athens. Dr Papadimitriou expressed strong interest in having HAPA participate in the 2008 Hellenic Psychiatric Association meeting in Crete on 14 May 2008, right after the APA Annual Meeting of 3–8 May 2008.

The officers discussed options for HAPA participation and agreed that HAPA sponsor two programmes at the Crete meeting: a panel discussion on postgraduate psychiatric education — “Postgraduate psychiatric training: options for training in the USA and Greece (or the EU)”, which Dr Lymberis offered to chair with both HAPA and HPA members; and a lecture by Dr Cassimatis, the incoming HAPA President, on a topic of his choice, with discussants to be determined by the HPA, preferably psychiatrists from Greece.

The officers discussed the May 2008 HAPA Annual Meeting. The programme has been finalised for Tuesday 6 May 2008, with UCLA Professor George Bartzokis, MD speaking on “Brain aging and age-related risk factors for prevalent neurodegenerative disorders: implications for treatment and prevention”.

Dr Petrides will report next time on his efforts to obtain an educational grant for the CME annual meeting. Dr Lymberis will again apply to the APA and reserve a room for the 9th Annual Meeting on 6 May 2008 at 7:00 PM, again a dinner meeting. This meeting should have better attendance than last year's, but we need to work on getting the word out and getting more members to the meeting.

Dr Petrides also reported on an email from Dr George Dangas, President of the Hellenic Medical Society of New York, concerning the June 2007 Declaration of Kos of the Global Hellenic Medical Network and information about their future meetings. Members of the Executive Committee were asked to consider endorsing the Kos Declaration; it was agreed that they would review it and be prepared to vote at the next meeting.

The last issue discussed was nominations for HAPA officers for the May 2008 elections. The Chair of the Nominating Committee is Dr Cassimatis, who is currently receiving nominations.

The next Executive Committee meeting is planned for 26 November 2007 at 5:00 PM EST, to be chaired by Dr Petrides.

Respectfully submitted,
Emmanuel Cassimatis, MD
HAPA President-Elect

title.en: The Hellenic Psychiatric Association celebrates its 15th anniversary
title.el: Η Ελληνική Ψυχιατρική Εταιρεία γιορτάζει τα 15 χρόνια της

summary.en: December 12, 2000, Athens — the HPA marked fifteen years at the Aula of the University of Athens, with honorary diplomas and a review of the journal Psychiatriki.
summary.el: 12 Δεκεμβρίου 2000, Αθήνα — η ΕΨΕ γιόρτασε τα δεκαπέντε της χρόνια στην Αίθουσα Τελετών του Πανεπιστημίου Αθηνών.

body.en:
December 12, 2000, Athens, Greece

The Hellenic Psychiatric Association (HPA) celebrated its 15th Anniversary on December 12, 2000 at the Aula of the University of Athens. The President of the Association, Professor George Christodoulou, introduced Professor George Babiniotis, the Rector of Athens University, Professor Christina Spiraki, the Minister of Health, the representative of Archbishop Christodoulos, the representative of the Mayor of Athens and Professor Juan Enrique Mezzich, the Secretary General of the World Psychiatric Association.

All speakers underlined the contribution of the Hellenic Psychiatric Association to the promotion of mental health in Greece and emphasized the Association's achievements with reference to postgraduate psychiatric education, organizing Panhellenic Psychiatric Congresses every two years, de-institutionalization of chronic psychiatric patients, consultation and advice to the Ministry of Health, publication of the journal Psychiatriki and various bulletins and informative leaflets for the public, and representation of Greek psychiatry to various international psychiatric organizations.

Among the issues discussed during the meeting by the president of the Hellenic Psychiatric Association, Professor Christodoulou, were the work of the two main peripheral branches in Athens and Thessaloniki and of the five Sections of the Association (Biological Psychiatry, Psychophysiology, Child Psychiatry, Psychotherapy and Social Psychiatry). Also discussed were the international relationships of the Association with various psychiatric associations. He specifically noted the relationships of the HPA with the World Psychiatric Association, the European Board on Psychiatry and the Hellenic American Psychiatric Association.

Professor Christodoulou also delivered honorary diplomas of distinction to members of the Association who had contributed greatly to its work: Professor G. Lyketsos; Professor E. Dimitriou; Professor A. Paraschos; Dr D. Malliaras; Dr J. Pittaras; Dr N. Zachariadis; and Dr Chr. Varouchakis. Professor M. Markidis, Editor of Psychiatriki, the official journal of the Association, reviewed the achievements of the journal during its first ten years of publication. Professor V. Kontaxakis, the Deputy Editor, announced that the editorial board had honoured Professor Christodoulou's contributions by awarding him the title of Honorary Editor. Finally, as part of this special anniversary day, the new offices of the Hellenic Psychiatric Association were inaugurated at Papadiamantopoulou Street 11, 11528 Athens.

The celebration was very well attended — there were no empty seats. The meeting ended with a moving performance by the Athens University Chorus, conducted by A. Vassilakis.

Respectfully submitted,
George Christodoulou, MD
